Title: Singapore's UOB misses on Q3 profit, margin pressures loom; shares slide
Article:
SINGAPORE: United Overseas Bank (UOB) said on Wednesday its third-quarter net profit missed expectations and flagged further margin pressures ahead, sending its shares sliding.
The Singapore lender lowered the full-year outlook for its net interest margin (NIM), a key profitability gauge, as it expects funding costs will remain elevated.
UOB's net profit for the third quarter came in at S$1.25 billion (US$975.72 million), underperforming the mean estimate of S$1.35 billion from two analysts, according to LSEG data.
The profit was more than double that of a year earlier, but the year-ago quarter was a low base due to a surge in credit provisions by the bank.
UOB's shares sank more than 5.0 per cent to reach a nearly five-month low of S$38.15.
UOB Chief Financial Officer Leong Yung Chee said NIM for the full year is likely to fall below 1.75 per cent, down from the previous quarter's guidance of 1.75 per cent to 1.80 per cent.
For the third quarter, the bank's NIM narrowed 6 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 1.68 per cent due to higher funding costs.
Leong said this was due to "intense competition amongst banks for deposits being raised".
"Even though an external environment of firming interest rates, the pricing of asset yields versus the pricing up of cost of deposits were acting in different directions," he added.
The bank's trading and investment income slid 33 per cent from a year earlier to S$322 million, which it attributed to less favourable market conditions. That weighed on other non-interest income, which fell 29 per cent from a year earlier to S$370 million.
Growth in its wealth management franchise continued to cushion its bottom line. Net fee income jumped 19 per cent from a year earlier to a record S$733 million, helped by strong growth in wealth, cards and loan-related activities.
Wealth management fees reached a record S$258 million in the third quarter, with net new money totalling S$5 billion in the first nine months of 2026.
For its 2027 outlook, the lender said it expects loan growth to come in at a mid-single-digit range, while it forecasts net interest income to be above 2026's levels. Meanwhile, it expects fee income to reach mid- to high-single-digit growth.
UOB has kicked off the third-quarter earnings season for Singapore banks, with larger peers DBS and OCBC due to report results on Thursday and Friday, respectively.

Title: MACC remands three, including Datuk, over RM1mil cigarette smuggling bribes
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Three people, including a company owner with a Datuk title, have been remanded over allegations that they paid RM1 million in bribes to police officers to protect cigarette smuggling activities.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said the suspects were believed to have acted as intermediaries, channelling bribes to several policemen to ensure no enforcement action was taken against cigarette smuggling operations in the East Coast states and the Klang Valley.
The suspects comprise a male company owner and two women, who work as a tuition teacher and a marketing officer. They are aged between their 30s and 50s.

Title: SPNB seeks private sector partnerships to reduce RMR housing waiting lists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Syarikat Perumahan Negara Bhd (SPNB) is exploring public-private partnerships to speed up the construction of Rumah Mesra Rakyat (RMR) homes and reduce waiting lists nationwide.
Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the initiative would involve government agencies, government-linked companies (GLCs) and private firms amid high demand for affordable housing.
She said the proposed collaborations would help SPNB increase its construction capacity beyond the government's annual RM500 million funding ceiling.
"SPNB is exploring strategic collaborations with government agencies, GLCs and the private sector to increase the implementation capacity of the RMR programme.
"Demand for RMR homes remains high, but the government's annual allocation is capped at RM500 million.
"Through these collaborations, we hope to accelerate the delivery of RMR homes and reduce waiting lists," she told the Dewan Rakyat.
She was responding to supplementary questions from Datuk Seri Dr Ismail Abd Muttalib (PN-Maran).
Aiman Athirah said the RM500 million allocation was the highest since the programme was introduced under the Eighth Malaysia Plan, compared with previous annual allocations of between RM300 million and RM400 million.
She said the RMR programme helped low-income households, particularly those in the B40 group, obtain safe and affordable housing.
The programme is open to Malaysians with monthly household incomes of RM5,000 or below who do not own a home or whose existing homes are dilapidated.
Eligible applicants must own land or obtain permission to build on family-owned land, subject to the programme's requirements.
Responding to the original question from Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong) on housing allocations, approvals and construction for B40 households and young families in Bentong, Aiman Athirah said SPNB had implemented 26,260 RMR units nationwide under the 12th Malaysia Plan.
Of these, 2,774 units were in Pahang, involving RM213.14 million and accounting for 10.56 per cent of the national total.
She said Pahang ranked fifth in RMR implementation, with 131 units built in Bentong.
However, 769 applicants remained on the waiting list in Pahang, with demand expected to increase.
Under the 2024 programme, Pahang received RM44.6 million to build 650 RMR units.
Of the 550 applications approved at the time, 547 homes had been completed and three were under construction, while another 100 applications were undergoing final screening.
In Bentong, 25 applications were approved in 2024, with 24 homes completed and handed over to recipients and one nearing completion.
Young Syefura also raised concerns over completed homes lacking basic infrastructure, including water and electricity supply and drainage.
Aiman Athirah clarified that the RMR programme covered house construction, while supporting infrastructure was the responsibility of the relevant state government or applicant, depending on the arrangements.

Title: Princeton Digital secures RM5.1bil funding for Johor expansion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Princeton Digital Group has secured US$1.3 billion (RM5.1 billion) in green financing to support the continued development and expansion of its JH1 data centre campus in Johor.
The financing, underwritten by Affin Bank, HSBC, Maybank, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB, builds on funding secured for earlier phases of the campus in April 2024 and an upsized facility in October 2025.
The proceeds will be used to expand JH1, a 200-megawatt campus in Sedenak Tech Park designed to support high-density artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud workloads.
The facility is structured under Princeton Digital's Green Finance Framework and supports the development of JH1 in line with recognised green building standards.
The campus obtained Green Building Index Gold certification for design and LEED Gold certification for operations.
The transaction also advances Princeton Digital's plan, announced in March, to raise up to US$5 billion in debt financing to deliver contracted data centre capacity across Asia Pacific.
"This financing reflects the confidence of our banking partners, several of whom have supported JH1 since its earliest phases, in the group's execution capabilities and deep hyperscaler partnerships," said Rangu Salgame, Princeton Digital chairman, chief executive officer and co-founder.
The company entered Johor in 2023 and has continued to focus on local talent development and community engagement through partnerships with local organisations.
Backed by global institutional investors including Warburg Pincus, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, Mubadala and Stonepeak, Princeton Digital has a portfolio exceeding 1.8 gigawatts across eight Asia Pacific countries.

Title: New Zealand votes with economy, cost of living in focus
Article:
WELLINGTON: New Zealanders are voting this week in an election focused on rising costs of living and the economy, as pollsters forecast a tight contest and neither main party close to winning a majority.
Prime Minister Christopher Luxon is hoping his right-wing coalition can cling to power with a message of "no new taxes" and by painting his opponents as an unpredictable alliance of left-wingers.
But the opposition Labour Party is banking that voter worries about costs of living will see it returned to office.
Here's what you need to know about the poll:
- What are the key issues? -
The cost of living is the biggest issue for voters, according to the RNZ-Reid Research Poll run by New Zealand's public broadcaster.
Sixty-four per cent of respondents said inflation and rising costs were their biggest concerns, followed by the state of New Zealand's healthcare system and then petrol prices.
The economy and rising unemployment rounded out the top five issues, according to the poll.
- Who's running? -
Luxon, a millionaire businessman-turned-politician, has led his National Party to worrying lows in polls and had to fend off two leadership challenges this year.
Luxon has told AFP he sees himself as a "super salesman" for the country and would push for more free-trade deals if re-elected.
His main opponent is Labour former Prime Minister Chris Hipkins, who succeeded Jacinda Ardern in 2023 and has seized on National's inability to curb the cost of living to revive his party's fortunes.
But with polls suggesting neither will win an outright majority in parliament, both will need help from minor parties to govern.
On the left, the Green Party has surged to record support by focusing on living costs, with plans to take on New Zealand's supermarket duopoly and impose a wealth tax on the country's richest residents.
On the right, populist Winston Peters and his NZ First – known for colourful and controversial language at home and abroad – have pledged swingeing cuts to immigration and to pull the country out of the Paris Climate Accord.
And the libertarian ACT party – led by former "Dancing With The Stars" contestant David Seymour – forms the third pillar of the right-wing alliance that has ruled New Zealand since 2023.
In the centre, Qiulae Wong of the Opportunity Party stands as a potential kingmaker, promising greater action on climate change and a kinder, more empathetic style of politics.
- When does the voting start and end? -
It's already begun.
New Zealanders have been able to cast their votes since October 26.
Saturday is the final day of voting, with polls set to close at 7:00 pm (0600 GMT).
An exit poll is expected to be released immediately.

Title: CGS International positive on Oriental Kopi's store roll-out in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CGS International Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd remains constructive on Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd's store roll-out as the group is on track to reach 40-41 Malaysian outlets by the end of 2026, up from 34 outlets as at July this year.
The brokerage said that with six mall locations already secured, Oriental Kopi's target of eight to 10 new outlets per annum looked achievable.
"With Oriental Kopi having already secured most high-footfall locations, it is now moving into second-tier malls.
"We think this should keep rental costs in check, while average paybacks of 10-12 months continue to support returns," said CGS International in a research note today.
The brokerage said Oriental Kopi's overseas segment would serve as a second growth engine, with its first outlet in Indonesia by end-November or early December this year, followed by Mauritius in the first quarter of next year, and two new outlets planned for Singapore in 2027, in addition to its three current outlets.
"We view execution risks as manageable given its measured rollout and potential use of local partners through a capital-light joint venture or franchise model in its overseas expansion," said CGS International.
The brokerage believed that its forecast of Oriental Kopi's core net profit of RM67.4 million for the financial year ended Sept 30, 2026, with a fourth quarter core net profit of RM22 million, driven by new-store contributions and stabilising gross profit margins, amid steady raw material prices.
Meanwhile, CGS International hosted Oriental Kopi's management and investors on Nov 3, 2026, to discuss its Oct 2026 menu language controversy.
"Management said that the matter has been resolved with its trilingual menus introduced in Nov 26 at a reprinting cost of RM150,000, with no material impact on footfall.
"The revised menu is now in use at the new Aman Central and Merdeka 118 outlets and should be rolled out to the remaining outlets by end-November this year," it said.
CGS International noted that Oriental Kopi's management said that it has not seen meaningful changes in traffic or customer mix following the controversy, and that the three outlets opened in the past 10 days in Sunway 163, Aman Central and Merdeka 118 have drawn long queues.

Title: Clear project purpose, investment readiness vital in viable regional connections
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Clear project objectives, investment readiness and commercial viability will be critical to translating Asean's renewable energy potential into viable cross-border electricity connections, says Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB).
Its chief grid officer, Datuk Ir. Hasmarizal Hassan, said regional interconnection projects must be supported by comprehensive feasibility studies, appropriate technology, committed electricity buyers and clearly defined investment decision points to ensure their long-term sustainability.
He said risks associated with such projects must be addressed progressively before final investment decisions, with competitive electricity costs remaining a key consideration in determining their commercial viability and ability to secure financing.
Hasmarizal highlighted these requirements during a panel discussion titled "Beyond the Cable: What Will It Take to Build a Sustainable Asean Power Market?" at the Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) 2026.
Malaysia's aspirations under the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), coupled with rising electricity demand, particularly from data centres, are increasing the need for greater renewable energy integration and regional connectivity.
Building on existing interconnections with Thailand and Singapore, TNB is advancing initiatives involving other Asean member states, including Singapore, Vietnam and Indonesia, to strengthen regional energy security and facilitate renewable electricity trade.
The initiatives are aligned with the broader Asean Power Grid (APG), a regional undertaking aimed at connecting the electricity networks of member states to enable greater cross-border power trading and enhance the reliability, affordability and sustainability of electricity supply.
Asean is targeting a fully integrated power grid by 2045, and the initiative is expected to require substantial investments in transmission infrastructure, domestic grid upgrades, and subsea electricity cables.
He said that through a disciplined approach to project development and investment planning, TNB continues to support the development of a sustainable APG, while creating opportunities for greater renewable energy utilisation and regional energy cooperation.
SIEW is an annual, high-level platform for energy professionals, policymakers, and commentators to discuss and share best practices within the global energy space.

Title: Stocks and dollar drop as Democrats enjoy big early wins
Article:
HONG KONG: Asian stocks fell with the dollar Wednesday, with the Democrats enjoying big early gains in the US midterms as they look to take control of both houses of Congress, which analysts said could lead to gridlock on Capitol Hill.
Tens of millions of Americans cast their vote in the crucial polls that have been pitched as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency amid anger at surging petrol prices, tariffs and the Iran war.
While Republicans were widely expected to lose control of the House, the Senate has been considered on a knife-edge, though the chances of a Democrat flip were boosted after they captured North Carolina.
The result handed Democrats a crucial gain in their bid to overcome the Republicans' 53-47 Senate majority.
A Democrat win would deal a hefty blow to Trump's agenda for his final two years in the White House, and analysts warned it would likely mean very little gets done in Washington in that time.
"A narrow blue wave may be largely priced in," said Chris Weston at Pepperstone. "A commanding one could force markets to rethink Trump's remaining policy agenda and the political trajectory into 2028.
"Democratic control of Congress would increase the potential for legislative gridlock, fiscal brinkmanship, debt-ceiling disputes, and congressional investigations."
However, he added that "the president would retain considerable executive authority, so the implications for individual sectors are far from straightforward".
Trump threatened in a telephone interview with the CBS network on Tuesday to be "Mr Veto" and block any Democratic legislation if they win.
Prediction markets indicated a "blue wave" for the Democrats, with Polymarket saying they were 100 percent likely to take the House and 99 percent to win the Senate.
The prospect of Congress coming to a standstill weighed on the dollar and Treasury yields, with observers pointing out that such a scenario would restrict spending.
"Typically, when we get a divided government, it has been historically pretty good for Treasuries," said Brij Khurana at Wellington Management.
Asian equity markets were also down, with Tokyo losing more than three percent as the yen spiked against the greenback, weighing on exporters.
There were also losses in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Seoul, Singapore and Taipei.
Tech firms were also under pressure as investors continue to fret over the AI investment boom and when firms that have pumped billions into the sector will eventually see returns, if ever.
In Tokyo, chipmaker Kioxia plunged more than 13 percent, while Advantest and SoftBank lost more than eight percent. And in Seoul, SK hynix shed as much as three percent, with Samsung almost two percent down.
Oil prices extended Tuesday's drop as investors kept tabs on the Middle East after Trump confirmed US strikes on Iran but played down speculation he was preparing to resume bombing after the election.

"I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it."
His Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue", adding that "no one will benefit from this war" if it reignited.
However, Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the Islamic republic was "ready for battle with its finger on the trigger", while Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Tehran retained the right to "legitimate self-defence".

Title: No instructions from Najib to settle RM50mil fine, says lawyer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyer, Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee, said he had received no instructions from his client to pay the RM50 million fine, which would allow him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
Farhan's presence at the Kuala Lumpur courts complex had fuelled speculation that the fine would be settled. However, he said he was there for another matter and had since been inundated with messages seeking clarification.
"I have no instructions and am unsure of the current status. I have not received any instructions regarding the fine.
"I definitely have no information. Even if a third party wants to make the payment, I would be expected to be informed," he told reporters at the lobby.
Najib's lead lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, who was also at the premises said he could not say whether the payment would be made in the coming days.
"I cannot predict. As far as I am concerned, as of today, there are no instructions," he told reporters.
Shafee said he was heading to the courts complex bookstore and dismissed the payment speculation as media-driven.
It remains unclear whether the fine will be paid today and, if so, who will make the payment and at what time.
Several media personnel are waiting in the courts complex lobby but have been barred from entering the payment counter area.
Police personnel have also been deployed to the lobby.
On Sept 18, Najib received a
conditional pardon
from Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Najib, 73, was sentenced to 12 years in jail and fined RM210 million after the Kuala Lumpur High Court found him guilty on July 28, 2020, of seven charges involving the misappropriation of RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.

Title: Gold firms on softer oil prices, US midterm results awaited
Article:
BENGALURU: Gold prices edged higher in early Asian trade on Wednesday as softer oil prices eased inflation concerns, while investors awaited US midterm election results and key labour market data for clues on the Federal Reserve's monetary policy direction.
Spot gold rose 0.2 per cent to US$3,934.75 an ounce by 12.24am GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.1 per cent to US$3,943.20.
Oil prices eased about one per cent on Tuesday to their lowest level in nearly four weeks, as the market weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against concerns that recent attacks in both conflicts could further disrupt supplies.
Russia will hold three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi from Nov 10 to 11, the Kremlin confirmed on Tuesday.
However, Iran and the United States remain far from reaching a deal to end their war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, as mediator Qatar stepped up efforts to bridge differences and avert a renewed escalation after the US midterm elections.
Lower oil prices ease inflation concerns and reinforce expectations that the Federal Reserve may not need to keep interest rates elevated for an extended period, boosting the appeal of non-yielding bullion.
Investors were bracing for a potentially strong showing by Democrats in Tuesday's midterm elections, which could pave the way for greater volatility in asset prices.
Traders currently see a 78 per cent chance of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Elsewhere, India's gold demand is expected to fall to a six-year low in 2026 as elevated prices weigh on jewellery sales and investment demand moderates, the World Gold Council (WGC) said on Tuesday.
Among other precious metals, spot silver fell 0.2 per cent to US$49.67 an ounce, while platinum rose 0.3 per cent to US$1,422.15 and palladium gained 0.5 per cent to US$938.49.

Title: Da'i Syed's final appeal against rape conviction to be decided today
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal here is scheduled to deliver its decision today on celebrity preacher Da'i Syed's final appeal to set aside his conviction and 10-year prison sentence and three strokes of the cane for rape.
The three-member panel, chaired by Datuk Azman Abdullah, is scheduled to sit with Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid to hear the final appeal by Da'i Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, 31.
Syed Shah Iqmal, dressed in a white robe and accompanied by his wife, Hana Ismail, arrived at the court at 8.55am.
On Dec 10, 2020, Syed Shah Iqmal pleaded not guilty to raping a 23-year-old woman at the time in a condominium room in I-City, Section 7, at 1.35am on Sept 11, 2019.
The charge was brought under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
On April 10, 2023, the Shah Alam Sessions Court acquitted and discharged Syed Shah Iqmal after ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him at the close of its case.
However, the Shah Alam High Court subsequently allowed the prosecution's appeal and ordered him to enter his defence against the charge.
On Aug 30, 2024, Sessions Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid sentenced him to 10 years in prison and three strokes of the cane.
He was ordered to begin serving his sentence on the same day.
After spending 21 days at Kajang Prison, Syed Shah Iqmal was temporarily released by the High Court here pending the hearing of his main appeal to set aside his conviction and sentence.

Title: China's services growth slows to three-month low as confidence weakens
Article:
BEIJING: China's services activity in October expanded at its slowest pace since July, with business confidence easing as firms grappled with fierce competition and rising costs, a private-sector survey showed on Wednesday.
The RatingDog China General Services PMI fell to 50.8 in October from 51.6 in September, remaining above the 50 mark that separates growth from contraction but marking its weakest reading since July.
New business continued to grow at a rate broadly unchanged from September.
New export business rose for the sixth straight month, extending the longest growth streak seen since 2024.
Services firms continued to add both full- and part-time staff to cope with existing workloads.
However, increased competition led services firms to lower their average selling prices for the second month, with the week-long Golden Week holiday offering little support.
Input prices increased at the quickest pace in five months, driven by higher input material, fuel and wage costs.
Business confidence slipped to its lowest since July, with firms citing concerns over rising input prices and heightened competition.

Title: Bursa Malaysia opens higher but reverses early gains amid cautious sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index opened higher but retreated thereafter, tracking cautious sentiment across regional markets amid mixed overnight cues from Wall Street.
At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) decreased 3.13 points to 1,618.72 from yesterday's close of 1,621.85.
The benchmark index opened 1.46 points higher at 1,623.31.
In the broader market, losers led gainers 160 to 122, while 273 counters were unchanged, 2,206 untraded, and 10 suspended.
Turnover stood at 138.01 million units worth RM56.89 million.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Wall Street ended mixed, with market attention focused on the US midterm elections, amid expectations of a potential sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks should the Democrats gain control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.
Regionally, sentiment was buoyed by China's commitment to expand yuan liquidity in Hong Kong, alongside better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 gross domestic product growth, he said.
"On the home front, the FBM KLCI was up slightly to above the 1,620 level yesterday as stock accumulation from foreign funds continues.
"Though overall trading was rather muted, it is heartening to see the net inflow of foreign funds of late. Thus, for today, we anticipate the index to trend within a narrow range of 1,615-1,625," he told Bernama.
Among the heavyweight stocks, Maybank and CIMB fell five sen each to RM9.99 and RM6.93, respectively. Public Bank was flat at RM4.81, while Tenaga Nasional increased two sen to RM13.18 and IHH Healthcare added one sen to RM7.77.
In active trade, Aizo rose one sen to eight sen, Dagang Nexchange, Bina Puri and Zetrix AI inched up half a sen each to 41 sen, 22 sen and 6.5 sen, respectively. NWE Resources was flat at 20 sen.
MISC led the top gainers, gaining 12 sen to RM8.47, while KLCC rose eight sen to RM8.38, Malayan Cement bagged six sen to RM5.36, while Pentamaster and Master Tec improved five sen each to RM5.32 and RM1.10, respectively.
Among the top losers, United Plantations decreased 20 sen to RM29.68, Hong Leong Bank dropped 18 sen to RM21.16, and Telekom Malaysia fell nine sen to RM7.81. Westports and Sunway Construction lost eight sen each to RM7.19 and RM7.64, respectively.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index decreased 20.0 points to 12,048.32, while the FBM Top 100 Index trimmed 20.72 points to 11,859.13.
The FBM Mid 70 Index sank 20.86 points to 17,298.04, the FBM Emas Shariah Index was 14.09 points lower at 12,030.82, and the FBM ACE Index gave up 0.82 points to 5,318.22.
Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.07 points to 177.65, the Energy Index inched up 0.76 points to 827.76, the Financial Services Index narrowed 68.69 points to 18,648.21, and the Plantation Index lost 6.21 points to 8,763.44.

Title: New Zealand jobless rate hits 11-year high in run-up to polls
Article:
WELLINGTON: New Zealand's unemployment rate climbed to an 11-year high in the third quarter, underscoring the economic and inflation pressures dominating the country's election campaign and sharpening the challenge for Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who is seeking another term.
Luxon's centre-right National Party-led coalition is facing mounting pressure to demonstrate that its policies can lift growth and ease cost-of-living strains, with a Ipsos poll earlier this week listing inflation and the cost of living as the top concern for voters ahead of a tight election contest on November 7.
The jobless rate rose to 5.7 per cent in the three months to September, its highest since 2015, from 5.5 per cent in the previous quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday. Employment fell 0.1 per cent from the prior quarter.
Barbara Edmonds, finance spokesperson for the opposition Labour Party, described the jobs numbers as "a damning verdict on Christopher Luxon's economic management."
"His last chance to show his plan was working has come and gone, and Kiwis are paying the price...For working families, the pressure hasn't let up. The cost of living is still biting, bills are piling up and wages are struggling to keep pace," she said in a statement.
Finance Minister and National Party parliamentarian Nicola Willis said the data reflects the impact of uncertainty on the economy and the need to stick with the current government's plan, which she believes is working to rebuild the economy.
Luxon, the former Air New Zealand chief executive officer, beat Labour leader Chris Hipkins in the 2023 election, promising to lower debt, bring down inflation and drive growth in the economy.
Even though economists say there are signs that the economy has started to recover, unemployment has tracked higher and it did not peak in the second quarter as the central bank had forecast.
The labour figures on Wednesday were weaker than market expectations, with economists in a Reuters poll forecasting unemployment of 5.5 per cent and a 0.4 per cent increase in employment. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand had also forecast a 5.5 per cent jobless rate.
The weaker data saw the New Zealand dollar dip before returning to trade largely unchanged at USUS$0.5592, while two-year swap rates fell 6.0 basis points to 3.7815 per cent.
The participation rate slipped to 70.4 per cent, below forecasts of 70.7 per cent.
Wage growth also moderated, adding to signs that the economy is losing momentum. The private-sector labour cost index, excluding overtime, rose 0.4 per cent in the quarter, slowing from a 0.7 per cent increase in the previous three months. Annual wage growth eased to 2.0 per cent from 2.1 per cent in the second quarter.
IMPLICATIONS FOR CASH RATE
The figures could lessen pressure on the central bank to resume interest-rate increases after it surprised markets last week by keeping the official cash rate unchanged at 2.75 per cent. The Reserve Bank said it wanted time to assess the impact of its two previous rate hikes, though it signalled further increases were still likely.
Kiwibank economists said the decision to hold rates looked increasingly justified as the labour market weakened.
"A weak labour market acts as a pressure lid on price growth … and we are seeing it play out in real time," they said in a note, adding that further rate increases would not be necessary if the trend continued.
Currently, the central bank has a single mandate to focus on inflation but employment does remain a component of decisions. However, Labour has promised that if it is elected then the central bank will be returned to a dual mandate where it considers price stability along with maximum sustainable unemployment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Orkim's early vessel delivery to drive earnings growth: analysts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Orkim Bhd has taken delivery of its 21st vessel, MT Orkim Jade, ahead of schedule, a development expected to bring forward its earnings contribution and strengthen revenue visibility, according to RHB Research.
The 2026-built clean petroleum products tanker has a carrying capacity of 14,500 deadweight tonnes (DWT), lifting Orkim's total fleet capacity by 5.4 per cent to 281,534 DWT.
The vessel is expected to begin commercial operations this month, supported by a long-term consecutive voyage charter with Shell Malaysia.
RHB maintained its "Buy" recommendation on Orkim with an unchanged target price of RM1.14, implying a potential upside of 46 per cent from its market price of 78 sen, alongside an estimated dividend yield of seven per cent.
"The early delivery is positive, bringing forward earnings contribution and providing greater earnings visibility," the research firm said.
RHB added that Orkim aims to add another five vessels between 2027 and 2029 as part of its fleet rejuvenation programme, which is expected to improve vessel quality, operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness.
Orkim remains on track to dispose of Orkim Fortune in the second half of 2026, which would bring its fleet capacity to about 274,200 DWT by year-end, followed by the expected delivery of Orkim Ruby in 2027.
These additions will be partly offset by the planned disposals of Orkim Express and Orkim Harmony in the first half of 2027, estimated to fetch RM20.8 million and RM13.4 million respectively.
Following the disposals, fleet capacity is expected to stand at about 273,400 DWT across 19 vessels by end of the financial year 2027 (FY27), before increasing to 20 vessels in FY28 and 21 vessels in FY29.
Separately, Apex Securities initiated coverage on Orkim with a "Buy" recommendation and a target price of RM1.26, representing a potential capital upside of 57.5 per cent, including an estimated FY27 dividend yield of 7.1 per cent.
Apex said the group's fleet renewal programme would help address concerns over its ageing vessels, with a sizeable portion of the existing fleet approaching 20 years of age.
It noted that the recent additions of Orkim Garnet, delivered in May 2026, and Orkim Opal, which began commercial operations in October 2026, had partly mitigated these concerns.
Together with the anticipated deliveries of Orkim Jade and Orkim Ruby, Apex expects the group's fleet capacity to reach about 273,000 DWT by end-2027, after accounting for planned vessel disposals.
On the tax front, both research firms highlighted the extension of the shipping income tax exemption under Budget 2027 as a positive development for Orkim's earnings visibility.
RHB said the extension provided greater clarity on the group's tax outlook, removing uncertainty surrounding the continuation of the incentive.
It expects Orkim's effective tax rate to remain at about two per cent, subject to continued compliance with the relevant eligibility requirements.
Meanwhile, Apex said; "Orkim's tax exemption on shipping income was initially scheduled to lapse after the year of assessment 2026 (YA2026), potentially subjecting a large portion of its shipping earnings to the statutory tax rate of 24 per cent.
"However, we believe the full income tax exemption announced under Budget 2027 effectively removes this earnings overhang, providing greater earnings visibility moving forward," it added.
It expects the group to maintain an effective tax rate of about one per cent following the extension.
Apex also highlighted Orkim's long-term charter agreements as a buffer against elevated fuel costs amid the Middle East conflict.
It said contractual arrangements, including time charters where charterers bear bunker costs and consecutive voyage charters and contracts of affreightment that allow monthly bunker cost adjustments, helped protect the group's earnings from rising fuel expenses.
The research firm added that Orkim could benefit from higher daily charter rates when existing contracts are renewed or extended, although its long-term charter profile also limits immediate exposure to prevailing freight rates.
RHB made no changes to its earnings forecasts, projecting recurring net profit of RM89 million for FY26, RM95 million for FY27 and RM99 million for FY28.
Apex, meanwhile, based its RM1.26 target price on a discounted cash flow valuation, using a weighted average cost of capital of 7.9 per cent and a terminal growth rate of two per cent.
Among the key risks identified by RHB were weaker demand for refinery products, piracy and armed robbery, lower daily charter rates, unscheduled maintenance, higher repair costs and geopolitical conflicts.
Apex also flagged customer concentration involving Petroliam Nasional Bhd and Shell, charter-rate and vessel utilisation risks as the tanker market normalises, delivery and funding risks associated with the fleet renewal programme, and potential policy changes to the shipping tax exemption beyond YA2036.

Title: Kerjaya Prospek set to ride power infrastructure boom
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd is poised to benefit from robust project flows in the power infrastructure segment, according to Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB).
This is supported by higher capital expenditure by Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), accelerating data centre developments and solar infrastructure investments.
The firm said the group's entry into the power infrastructure segment through a maiden contract win from TNB positions it to tap Malaysia's growing investment cycle.
The RM568.2 million contract, secured through a joint venture with Jati Tinggi Holdings Bhd and Betapac Sdn Bhd, involves the development of a transmission main intake substation in Paka, Terengganu.
Under the arrangement, Kerjaya Prospek will undertake the core and shell works with a 25 per cent stake, translating into an estimated RM142.1 million in revenue over two years.
HLIB said the contract brings Kerjaya Prospek's outstanding order book to about RM6 billion and year-to-date job replenishment to RM3.5 billion, providing strong earnings visibility alongside a healthy tender pipeline of about RM2 billion.
Kerjaya Prospek's 31 per cent stake in ES Sunlogy further broadens its exposure to the segment, opening up opportunities in mechanical and electrical engineering works.
On valuation, HLIB said Kerjaya Prospek trades at 13.8 times and 12.6 times its forecast financial year 2027 and 2028 earnings, respectively, below its three-year historical average of 14.3 times and the peer average of 18.8 times and 16.5 times.
It said the valuation was supported by an estimated 15.1 per cent compound annual growth rate in earnings per share between FY26 and FY28, alongside projected dividend yields of 4.0 to 4.5 per cent over the same period.
From a technical perspective, HLIB said Kerjaya Prospek's share price had undergone healthy profit-taking after rallying 82 per cent from its year-to-date low of RM2.06 to RM3.74 before rebounding to RM3.46 on elevated trading volume.
The stock has reclaimed its 20-day moving average and formed a higher low, suggesting its upward momentum is regaining traction.
A decisive breakout above RM3.60, its September 11 high, could pave the way for a retest of RM3.74, its year-to-date peak, and potentially RM3.98, based on the 114 per cent Fibonacci retracement level.
HLIB identified support levels at RM3.41, RM3.35 and RM3.15, corresponding to the 20-day moving average, 50-day moving average and October low, respectively, with a stop-loss level at RM3.21.

Title: Oil edges down as investors await US midterm election results
Article:
BEIJING: Oil prices slipped in early trade on Wednesday as investors awaited the results of the US midterm elections and their potential impact on peace talks in the Middle East, even as industry data showed US crude inventories unexpectedly fell last week.
Brent crude futures fell 26 cents, or 0.25 per cent, to US$103.34 a barrel by 1.57am GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 53 cents, or 0.55 per cent, to US$95.56.
In the previous session, Brent fell more than one per cent to its lowest level in nearly four weeks as traders weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
Vote counting was underway in the US midterm elections, which will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republican Party retains control of Congress for the remainder of his second term.
Markets remained alert to any progress in talks to end the US-Israeli war with Iran, as Qatar stepped up mediation efforts to avert an escalation in attacks after the US midterm elections.
A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran and the United States remained far from reaching a deal to end their war.
The United States carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm island targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said on Tuesday. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.
US President Donald Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday that the United States had no immediate plans to strike Iran.
"We seem to be getting everything we want," Trump said in a six-minute telephone interview.
Meanwhile, crude inventories fell by 5.27 million barrels in the week ended Oct 30, market sources said on Wednesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
Eight analysts polled by Reuters had expected crude inventories to rise by an average of about 880,000 barrels.
Gasoline inventories rose by 1.43 million barrels, while distillate inventories fell by 1.19 million barrels from a week earlier, the sources said.
"Diesel inventories remain tight, while gasoline stocks rose more than expected. The data are broadly supportive of oil prices," Haitong Futures said in a note on Wednesday.
Official data from the US Energy Information Administration is due at 10.30am EST (3.30pm GMT) on Wednesday.

Title: Overlapping jurisdictions hamper monitoring of halal slaughterhouses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Overlapping jurisdictions among government ministries, departments and agencies have made it difficult to monitor slaughterhouse operations and enforce halal certification compliance, potentially allowing breaches of Islamic requirements.
The division of responsibilities among multiple agencies, each overseeing different aspects of operations, has also highlighted the absence of a comprehensive coordination mechanism to ensure halal compliance throughout the chicken supply chain.
The Department of Veterinary Services (DVS), for instance, handles applications for slaughterhouse construction and operating licences, including renewals.
The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, meanwhile, focuses on enforcing trade integrity laws, including the sale of wholesale chicken without valid scheduled controlled goods permits and the misuse of halal logos or certificates.
The Health Ministry is responsible for ensuring hygiene and food safety standards are met, including preventing livestock products from being contaminated by bacteria or toxins before reaching consumers.
The Environment Department (DOE) monitors waste management at slaughterhouses to prevent environmental pollution, particularly water contamination caused by the discharge of wastewater and animal blood.
Local authorities are also responsible for ensuring premises have valid business permits and comply with requirements on hygiene, waste management and slaughterhouse operations.
Religious authorities, including state Islamic religious departments and the Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim), oversee compliance with Islamic requirements, halal certification and enforcement relating to halal status.
Jakim said slaughterhouse operations fell under the jurisdiction of several authorities because they involved various processes, including slaughtering, hygiene, food safety, halal certification compliance and premises licensing.
It said integrated coordination in inspections and enforcement operations was therefore necessary among the relevant authorities, including local councils, DVS, ministries and state religious authorities, to strengthen oversight and curb slaughterhouse activities that violated Islamic requirements.
More concerningly, existing laws do not require all slaughterhouse operators to obtain a Malaysian Halal Certification (SPHM), creating a gap between permission to operate and official halal verification.
Jakim told Berita Harian that operating licences and halal certification served different purposes.
An operating licence allowed premises to conduct business subject to the relevant authorities' conditions, while SPHM verified compliance with Malaysia's halal certification requirements.
"Having an operating licence alone does not mean that a slaughterhouse is halal-certified," the religious authority said.
The regulatory gaps have come under renewed scrutiny following a raid on a chicken slaughterhouse warehouse in Puchong, Selangor, under Ops Taring Chiller recently.
Commenting on the issue, Muafakat Ilmuan Islam (Muis) senior fellow Bilal Jailani said the current halal crisis stemmed from an overly cautious legislative approach, leaving Muslim consumers exposed to the risk of buying raw chicken with uncertain halal status.
He said that despite Malaysia pioneering halal certification in 1974, the country still lacked a firm enforcement framework requiring certification at slaughterhouses, wholesale and retail levels, as well as for commercial food products.
He said it was time to review the voluntary halal certification approach and consider making certification mandatory across a wider range of food industry operators.
"The root of this crisis is that our halal legislation has been too cautious. Applications for halal certification indeed remain voluntary, but after decades, the time has come to make it mandatory," he said.
Meanwhile, Putrajaya member of parliament Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin also raised concerns over the halal status of raw chicken sold in the market.
In a post on his official Facebook account yesterday, he said the issue needed to be addressed through a comprehensive monitoring and enforcement framework covering the halal chicken and meat supply chains.

Title: Suhakam to meet Perak govt over monastery demolition dispute
Article:
IPOH: The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) will meet the Perak government over alleged human rights violations linked to a threat to demolish the Sakyamuni Cave Monastery in Gunung Kanthan here for quarrying activities.
Suhakam commissioner Abdul Kadir Jailani Ismail said the move followed a memorandum submitted by the monastery's monks on Aug 27, alleging restricted access and intimidation, including surveillance by drones.
He said the meeting with the state government would take place after Suhakam completed a comprehensive report based on findings and feedback from eight agencies involved in the dispute.
"Suhakam is mandated to provide views and advice to state governments on human rights issues. We also have the authority to conduct monitoring.
"We will examine the problems, the actions taken by the relevant agencies, the underlying causes and possible solutions.
"Following discussions at our monthly meeting, we will determine the main issues and whether there have been actual human rights violations. The next step is to engage with the Perak government," he said after visiting the monastery yesterday.
Also present were the monastery's head monk, Bhante Kusala; its lawyer, Leong Cheok Keng; and Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM) field researcher Meor Razak Meor Abdul Rahman.
The dispute involves the approximately 100-year-old Buddhist monastery and a cement company, with issues including land rights, eviction, freedom of religion and environmental conservation.
Abdul Kadir said the visit was intended to give Suhakam a clearer understanding of the situation, particularly the alleged human rights violations outlined in the memorandum.
He said Suhakam, as a commission established under parliament, was responsible for looking into complaints involving human rights and referring relevant matters to the appropriate agencies for further action.
Meanwhile, Kusala alleged that the rights of the monastery's residents and visitors had been violated through restrictions on their movements, including having to register every time they entered or left the premises.
He also claimed their privacy had been compromised by the use of drones to monitor their movements.
Kusala described the restrictions as arbitrary detention, saying they had been imposed before the court had reached a final decision, with an appeal still pending at the Court of Appeal and an application to stay the execution of the court's decision awaiting hearing.
"In June, they placed concrete barriers at the monastery's main entrance, preventing members of the public from entering.
"Our movements are constantly monitored, as though they are trying to pressure us into leaving.
"On the worst days, drones are flown at very low altitudes up to three times a day to monitor and track our movements within the monastery," he said.

Title: Najib to pay RM50mil fine today for house arrest release
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak is reportedly set to pay the RM50 million fine imposed on him to enable him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
A source said the fine would be paid by a representative of Najib at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex today.
On Sept 18, the former Pekan member of parliament received a conditional pardon from Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Najib, 73, was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million after being found guilty by the Kuala Lumpur High Court on July 28, 2020, on seven charges involving the misappropriation of RM42 million in funds belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.

Title: Two men killed, woman injured in separate Penang road crashes
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Two men died and a woman injured in two separate road crashes in Penang between late Tuesday night and early Wednesday morning.
In the first incident at 11.38pm, a Rapid bus and a Modenas Z250 motorcycle collided along Jalan Mayang Pasir, in front of Sunshine Square 1, Bayan Lepas.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said eight personnel from the Bayan Baru fire station were deployed to the scene after receiving an emergency call.
"Upon arrival, rescuers found two victims from the motorcycle. A 23-year-old woman, who was pinned in front of the bus, was extricated at 11.55pm and rushed to Penang Hospital by a community ambulance after receiving initial treatment.
"The second victim, a 29-year-old motorcyclist identified as Goy Wee Sherng, was trapped beneath the front of the bus. He was extricated at 12.30am and pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel," he said in a statement.
Francis said the bus driver escaped unhurt, adding that the deceased's body was handed over to the police for further action.
[[nid:1570299]]
Meanwhile, at 6.35am, firemen responded to a fatal single-vehicle crash at Seri Tanjung Pinang, near Straits Quay in Tanjung Tokong.
Six firefighters from the Bagan Jermal fire station were dispatched after a Toyota Vios skidded and crashed.
"A male driver in his 30s was found pinned and unconscious inside the driver's seat. Rescuers managed to extricate him at 6.55am, but he was confirmed dead at the scene by medical personnel," he added.
The victim's identity has yet to be ascertained.

Title: Sabah offers to host Malaysia's proposed nuclear energy hub
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah is prepared to be considered as a potential hub for Malaysia's proposed nuclear energy programme, said State Government Backbenchers Club (BBC) chairman Datuk Masiung Banah.
He said the state needed to prepare for rising electricity demand by 2031, while reducing its reliance on natural gas and diesel amid volatile global energy markets.
Masiung said Sabah's electricity supply capacity remained strained and lagged behind the development of utilities in Peninsular Malaysia.
"BBC sees the need for the Sabah government to prepare for a surge in electricity demand by 2031 and reduce dependence on natural gas and diesel amid volatile global markets.
"Therefore, Sabah is ready to propose itself as the first hub for this high-impact nuclear programme," he said in a statement.
He said the Sabah and Federal governments could work together to develop the programme, with negotiations pursued under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) framework.
Masiung's proposal follows Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof's remarks that Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia were the most practical locations for a
nuclear power plant
in the coming decades, should the country decide to pursue nuclear energy.
The Kuamut assemblyman also suggested that Malaysia consider floating nuclear power plants, saying their construction costs and timelines could offer greater flexibility and be suited to Sabah's extensive coastline.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's first female Education director-general Asiah Abu Samah dies at 89
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Sri Asiah Abu Samah, the country's first female Education director-general, died at KPJ Damansara Hospital at 5am today. She was 89.
Her death was confirmed by her niece, Shafinaz Shamsudin.
Shafinaz said the funeral arrangements, including the bathing and shrouding of the body, were scheduled to take place at 10am at Masjid At-Taqwa in Taman Tun Dr Ismail.
The funeral prayers will be held after the Zohor prayers before the deceased is laid to rest.
"The deceased will then be buried at the Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery," she said when contacted.
Asiah made history when she became the first woman appointed Education director-general on Nov 27, 1991.
She graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in History and a Diploma in Education from the University of Malaya, Singapore, in 1961, before beginning her career as a teacher at Penang Free School in Penang.
Throughout her career, she held various key positions, including at the Language Institute in Lembah Pantai, Tunku Kurshiah College in Seremban, and several divisions within the Education Ministry.
She was appointed Deputy Education director-general II before being promoted to Deputy Education director-general I in mid-1990.
She retired from the civil service as Education director-general in 1992.

Title: OPR hike to boost bank earnings, deposit rivalry a concern
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's banking sector could see improved net interest margins (NIM) and earnings from an anticipated 25-basis-point increase in the overnight policy rate (OPR) to 3.0 per cent in the first half of 2027.
However, intensifying deposit competition could limit the benefits, says Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB).
The firm estimates that the rate normalisation could lift banks' calendar year 2027 (CY27) NIM by between 1.9 and 6.2 basis points, translating into a 1.3 to 9.3 per cent increase in profit after tax and minority interests (PATAMI).
It said Malaysia's stronger-than-expected economic performance had reduced the need for the additional monetary support introduced through Bank Negara Malaysia's July 2025 OPR cut to 2.75 per cent, which was intended to cushion the economy against external uncertainties, including US tariffs.
Gross domestic product expanded by 6.0 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, while the advance estimate for the third quarter showed growth of 5.3 per cent.
Against this backdrop, HLIB's economics team expects a 25-basis-point OPR normalisation in the first half of 2027, likely towards the later part of the period.
For its analysis, the firm assumed the increase would take place in June 2027.
HLIB said all banks under its coverage would see a positive CY27 NIM uplift, although the magnitude would vary considerably depending on their funding structures and exposure to floating-rate loans.
Its sensitivity analysis showed that Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd could record the largest improvement of 6.2 basis points, followed by Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd and Public Bank Bhd at 5.8 basis points each.
RHB Bank Bhd was expected to see a 5.5-basis-point uplift, followed by Affin Bank Bhd at 5.1 basis points and AmBank (M) Bhd at 4.7 basis points.
Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) was projected to record a more moderate improvement of 3.3 basis points, while CIMB Group Holdings Bhd trailed at 1.9 basis points.
HLIB said the estimates represented the average NIM impact for CY27, incorporating both the initial benefit from asset repricing and the subsequent catch-up in funding costs.
The analysis assumes floating-rate loans are repriced within one month, while current account and savings account (CASA) funding costs take six to nine months to adjust, with a base case of 7.5 months.
The estimated PATAMI uplift ranges from 1.3 per cent to 9.3 per cent in CY27, although the relatively larger sensitivities for Bank Islam and Affin Bank partly reflect their smaller earnings bases.
HLIB said banks' ability to sustain the initial margin gains would depend on how effectively they manage funding costs amid intensifying deposit competition.
The median loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) across its coverage rose to 95.5 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 92.6 per cent in the first quarter of 2024, pointing to tighter liquidity conditions.
It added that most banks were also operating below their respective NIM peaks recorded since 2024, suggesting that a return to previous margin levels could prove increasingly difficult as competition for deposits accelerates funding-cost increases.
Despite the potential earnings boost, HLIB viewed the anticipated OPR increase as an incremental earnings tailwind rather than a catalyst for a broader sector re-rating.
It said the stronger economic backdrop underpinning its rate outlook should also support financing demand and asset quality, providing broader fundamental benefits beyond margin expansion.
The firm maintained its "Neutral" rating on the banking sector, noting that banking stocks were trading at 1.08 times forward price-to-book value.
This was broadly in line with their five-year average of 1.09 times, leaving limited room for a broad-based re-rating.
Nevertheless, HLIB saw selective opportunities following the recent sell-off, upgrading RHB Bank Bhd to "Buy" from "Hold" with a higher target price of RM8.40.
It said the bank's upcoming capital management plan provided further potential for capital returns, while its positive sensitivity to OPR normalisation strengthened its investment case.
The combination of attractive dividend yields, potential capital returns and positive rate sensitivity had made RHB's risk-reward sufficiently attractive.

Title: Flash floods shut NKVE, Elite, GCE stretches around Shah Alam [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Heavy overnight rain triggered flash floods along several major stretches around Shah Alam early this morning, forcing road closures on the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE), North-South Expressway Central Link (Elite), and Guthrie Corridor Expressway (GCE).
Highway concessionaire Plus Malaysia Bhd, in an update on X, said flash floods hit Km9.1 of the NKVE between Shah Alam and Subang at 4.07am.
All lanes in both directions were blocked, forcing northbound traffic from Bukit Raja to be diverted to Setia Alam. Southbound traffic from Subang was diverted to the Elite highway.
Earlier, at 3.20am, Plus said all lanes leading into the Shah Alam Toll Plaza were closed due to flash floods, with motorists advised to use alternative routes.
At 5.30am, Plus reported the closure of all lanes at the Shah Alam Interchange on the Elite highway between Seafield and Setia Alam. Traffic from Seafield heading towards Shah Alam was temporarily diverted to the Shah Alam Toll Plaza.
Meanwhile, Prolintas GCE said on X that flash floods hit the NKVE interchange at 5.42am. The concessionaire said Ramp B, Ramp C, and Ramp D were fully closed.
Motorists have been advised to follow instructions from traffic personnel and use alternative routes.
Separately, a post on Threads claimed a bridge near Jalan Gajah 16 heading towards Paya Jaras was damaged and impassable.
The user, @sabrinarzk__, who shared video footage of the scene, said the damage also affected the route for Paya Jaras residents heading to Kampung Kubu Gajah.

Title: Man dies after parang attack in Teluk Intan
Article:
TELUK INTAN: A man died after being attacked with parangs by three men outside a shop in Taman Banjar Jaya here yesterday afternoon.
Hilir Perak police chief Assistant Commissioner Chua Kok Lian said the victim died while receiving treatment at Teluk Intan Hospital following the 3.53pm incident.
"Initial investigations found that the victim was attacked by three men armed with parangs. The motive is still under investigation.
"A 27-year-old woman has been arrested to assist in the investigation," he said in a statement.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
The incident drew attention after a short video showing a bloodied man lying inside a business premises went viral on social media.
The footage also showed a woman beside the victim attempting to administer first aid, while the premises appeared ransacked, with bloodstains on the floor.
Those with information about the incident can contact the Hilir Perak police headquarters at 05-629 9222 or visit the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang tightens fireworks sales rules ahead of 2027 Chinese New Year
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has introduced stricter safety conditions for fireworks traders in Penang ahead of the 2027 Chinese New Year celebrations.
The rules include a ban on sales near petrol stations and additional licensing conditions to prevent incidents that could threaten public safety.
In a statement, MBPP said applications for the 2027 Chinese New Year Seasonal Temporary Stall Licence are open from today until Dec 31, while applications for the Seasonal Temporary Stall Licence for Fireworks Sales are open from today until Nov 30.
The operating period for seasonal temporary stalls is permitted from Jan 13 to Feb 20, 2027, while fireworks sales are only allowed from Jan 13 to Feb 11, 2027, subject to police conditions.
"The Seasonal Temporary Stall Licence and the Fireworks Sales Licence are two separate licences, and approval of a temporary stall licence does not automatically allow traders to sell fireworks.
"Traders intending to sell fireworks must obtain separate approval and permits from the police," MBPP said.
The council said traders are not allowed to operate near high-risk areas such as petrol stations or other locations deemed unsuitable by authorities. The sales location must also be approved by the council.
MBPP said traders must prepare suitable fire extinguishing equipment, ensure fireworks storage complies with safety conditions and police directives, and keep the sales area clean and free from unrelated flammable materials.
Smoking, burning, or testing fireworks at the sales site is strictly prohibited, while failure to produce or comply with police permits may result in the MBPP licence being revoked without further notice.
"All traders must comply with the approved site size and ensure business items, including chairs and tables, are placed within the permitted stall area to avoid obstructing the public.
"For food stalls, traders and assistants must have valid anti-typhoid vaccinations, avoid direct contact with food, and maintain personal hygiene at all times.
"The use of polystyrene containers for packaging or food displays is also prohibited. MBPP also encourages cashless transactions, the practice of bringing one's own bags, reducing single-use plastics, and adhering to the ban on plastic straws," MBPP said.
The council said foreigners are not permitted to apply for or operate businesses under either licence category.
It said any business activities conducted without MBPP approval or in breach of licence conditions will face appropriate action, including revocation of licences.
Both applications can be submitted online through the ulesen.mbpp.gov.my portal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt agencies ordered to strengthen readiness against cyber, supply threats
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: All ministries and government agencies have been directed to review their Business Continuity Plans (BCPs) to ensure critical government functions remain operational in the event of disruptions to the country's essential facilities.
Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the move was part of efforts to strengthen national security preparedness amid global uncertainty and geopolitical conflicts that could trigger various threats.
He said national security risk assessments must now take into account non-conventional threats, including cyberattacks, sabotage, disinformation and supply chain disruptions.
"Given the current global situation, marked by uncertainty and competing geopolitical interests, the government has a responsibility to assess threats that are no longer confined to conventional forms.
"Mechanisms must also be strengthened to address cyber threats, sabotage, disinformation and supply chain disruptions," he said in a Facebook post.
Shamsul Azri said ministries had also been directed to strengthen inter-agency coordination, information sharing and clarity of responsibilities to ensure swift action in the event of a threat.
He said the decision to review BCPs was aimed at ensuring essential government functions could continue if communication, energy, transportation or other critical infrastructure systems were disrupted.
The measures were in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's statement in Parliament yesterday on national security preparedness, he added.
Shamsul Azri said national sovereignty and security would not be compromised, with the government giving serious attention to risks that could affect national security, strategic sector interests and public safety.
Yesterday, Anwar told the Dewan Rakyat that the government was taking proactive steps to strengthen national preparedness in response to
rising global cyber threats
and geopolitical tensions, including ensuring adequate food, water and energy supplies.
He said a special National Security Council meeting had discussed existing mechanisms, tighter coordination among ministries, agencies and security forces, and measures to ensure the country was prepared for any eventuality.
Anwar also said several countries, including those in the European Union, Canada and Japan, had issued advisories urging their citizens to maintain basic food supplies for between three and 10 days.
He said international crises, including tensions in the Middle East, developments in Yemen and the Red Sea, and security threats in Europe, could have direct implications for public safety, economic stability and national interests.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning issued for eight states until 10am
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain, and strong wind warning for eight states until 10am today.
The weather warning affects Kedah (Kulim and Bandar Baharu) and Penang (Seberang Perai Selatan, Seberang Perai Tengah, Barat Daya, and Timor Laut).
Similar conditions are forecast in Perak (Kampar, Kinta, Kuala Kangsar, Bagan Datuk, Hulu Perak, Kerian, Larut Matang, Selama, Manjung, Perak Tengah, and Hilir Perak), Kelantan (Gua Musang), and Terengganu (Kemaman and Dungun).
The warning also covers Pahang (Cameron Highlands), Selangor (Sabak Bernam), and Sarawak (Sarikei covering Pakan, Julau, and Maradong; Mukah; Sibu; Kapit covering Song; Samarahan; Kuching; Serian; and Sri Aman).
MetMalaysia said warnings are issued when signs indicate thunderstorms with rainfall intensity exceeding 20 mm per hour that are imminent or expected to persist for more than an hour.
"A thunderstorm warning is a short-term advisory valid for no more than six hours per release," the department said in a statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Report: Najib will pay RM50m fine today to unlock house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is reportedly set to pay his RM50 million fine today, satisfying the core condition required to transfer him from Kajang Prison to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
Citing a source, the
New Straits Times
reported that a representative of the 73-year-old former premier is scheduled to deliver the payment at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex this morning.
Settling the financial penalty is the mandatory condition attached to the conditional pardon granted by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on Sept 18 during the 64th meeting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board at Istana Negara.
The royal decree permits Najib to serve the remainder of his reduced custodial term at home until Aug 23, 2028.
On Sunday, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said that the Attorney General’s Chambers had yet to receive proof of payment. Dusuki noted that while the pardon carried no fixed deadline for settlement, Najib was legally required to remain incarcerated in prison for as long as the fine stayed outstanding.
The fine forms part of Najib's conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd. The Kuala Lumpur High Court originally sentenced him in July 2020 to 12 years’ imprisonment and a RM210 million fine, penalties that were upheld by the Federal Court in August 2022.
The Pardons Board subsequently halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million during its 61st meeting on Jan 29, 2024.
Notwithstanding the house arrest, Najib still faces separate legal jeopardy from ongoing criminal and civil proceedings.
On Dec 26 last year, the High Court sentenced him to 15 years in prison and imposed an RM11.4 billion fine after convicting him of four counts of abuse of power and 21 counts of money laundering involving RM2.3 billion from 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), a verdict he appealed on Dec 29.
In a civil suit, the High Court on March 31 ordered Najib to repay US$1.3 billion to SRC International for breach of fiduciary duties. Enforcement of the order is stayed pending his appeal.
He also faces two other suits, filed by SRC International and Gandingan Mentari Sdn Bhd in 2021, as well as a US$5.64 billion civil suit by 1MDB and four of its subsidiaries. All remain before the courts.

Title: Finance Ministry: Malaysia seeks wider use of local currencies in cross-border trade through BRICS cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Malaysia aims to enhance the use of local currencies in cross-border trade and investment transactions through BRICS cooperation, thereby reducing transaction costs and foreign exchange risks.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said the move also aims to strengthen the country’s financial resilience against external shocks while providing businesses with more options for conducting international transactions.
It said wider use of local currencies could improve the efficiency of foreign exchange exposure management and support the development of regional foreign exchange markets.
“An increase in transactions using regional currencies, including those of BRICS member countries, could also enhance liquidity and support the development of regional foreign exchange markets, thereby providing businesses with more options,” the ministry stated to the Dewan Rakyat.
MoF was responding to Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang (PN-Marang) on reforms to the international financial system that Malaysia is pursuing through BRICS.
The ministry said Malaysia had also implemented various initiatives with major trading partners, including cooperation with China to facilitate the use of the renminbi and ringgit in bilateral trade.
Malaysia has also implemented the Local Currency Transaction Framework (LCTF) with Indonesia and Thailand.
The ministry said Malaysia would continue to strengthen and improve existing channels and mechanisms to facilitate and expand the use of local currencies in cross-border trade and investment.
However, it noted that the use of major currencies in international trade and finance remained driven by structural factors, including the size of financial markets and their widespread acceptance among businesses and investors.
“Therefore, efforts to expand the use of local currencies must be market-driven, supported by efficient cross-border payment infrastructure and continuous cooperation between countries,” MOF added. — Bernama

Title: Drop beer sponsor or lose permit, sports ministry warns Hyrox Kuala Lumpur organisers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The Youth and Sports Ministry has threatened to withhold event approval for the upcoming Hyrox Kuala Lumpur 2026 fitness race unless organisers completely cut ties with an alcoholic beverage sponsor.
The ministry issued the ultimatum following public scrutiny over a viral promotional graphic naming a commercial beer brand as the event’s “Official Beer Partner”. The multi-day fitness competition is scheduled to run from December 10 to 13 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec) in Kuala Lumpur.
Clarifying that the competition currently lacks legal sanction, the ministry confirmed that the organiser's licence application remains under review and that Putrajaya has neither approved the gathering nor disbursed any state funding.
Authorities cited Article 5.2 of the Safe Sport Code (3rd Edition, 2024), which strictly bars corporate entities involved in tobacco, e-cigarettes, and alcoholic beverages from sponsoring, advertising, merchandising, offering prizes, or affixing commercial trademarks across sports activities sanctioned or supported by the ministry and its agencies.
“The ministry will not compromise in ensuring a safe and healthy sports environment for all participants,” Youth and Sports Minister Mohammed Taufiq Johari said in a statement.
Under statutory licensing rules, prospective event promoters must formally pledge compliance with the Safe Sport Code before being granted regulatory clearance.
The ministry stressed that its position is non-negotiable: official operating permits will remain frozen until the alcohol sponsorship is terminated and all associated branding, logos, and promotional assets are completely purged from marketing channels and the Mitec competition floor.
Organisers were also reminded that staging an event without official sanction violates Section 36(1) of the Sports Development Act 1997, which bars companies from managing sports events without a licence issued by the Commissioner of Sports Malaysia. Breaching the statute carries penalties including fines between RM50,000 and RM500,000, up to five years in prison, or both.
Reiterating that the prohibition applies uniformly across all sporting disciplines without regard to commercial pedigree or target demographics, the ministry reaffirmed that fitness promotions must stay free of vice branding.

Title: Foreign AI election interference claims under Online Safety Act probe, ministry tells Parliament
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The federal government will deploy existing communications and cyber safety laws to counter an alleged foreign-linked artificial intelligence influence campaign targeting Malaysian electorates, while drafting a dedicated AI Governance Bill to establish regulatory oversight over developers, the Communications Ministry told Parliament.
The ministry disclosed this in a written parliamentary reply yesterday to Pasir Mas MP Tuan Haji Ahmad Fadhli Shaari, who questioned what steps the government would take to investigate foreign election meddling conducted through generative AI platforms, including  Claude.
The ministry confirmed that the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is treating the allegations seriously and has sought detailed technical clarification and supporting evidence from Anthropic, the US-based creator of Claude, to ensure any regulatory assessment is grounded in empirical findings.
Enforcement action will be pursued under the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 alongside the Online Safety Act 2025 and related statutes under MCMC's purview. The regulatory agency will coordinate with federal security bodies, criminal investigators, and social media platform providers where necessary.
In tandem with current enforcement tools, the Digital Ministry is drafting a standalone AI Governance Bill designed to codify corporate accountability, risk mitigation requirements, and developer liabilities across the artificial intelligence life cycle, though the reply offered no firm timeline for its introduction in Parliament.
The controversy originated from a threat intelligence report published in September by Anthropic, which revealed that a commercial actor had leveraged Claude to develop core components of a covert political influence campaign.
Anthropic attributed the activity to BBS Bilisim Teknolojileri, a technology firm based in Istanbul, noting that the operation attempted to construct synthetic persona networks, automated bot accounts, and bespoke propaganda websites.
The operation reportedly harvested demographic census records and voter data to profile electorates across all 222 federal parliamentary constituencies.
While the Turkish company denied involvement on September 11, Anthropic confirmed it had shuttered the offending accounts and noted that the campaign showed no evidence of gaining meaningful organic traction among genuine users.
Following the disclosures, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said urged authorities to mount a comprehensive and independent investigation.
However, the ministry did not disclose whether Anthropic has responded to MCMC's queries, whether police have registered a formal criminal investigation, or how existing domestic statutes can effectively hold offshore technology operators and foreign-based software firms accountable beyond Malaysian borders.

Title: Woman arrested over alleged harassment of visitors at Kuala Lumpur shopping mall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Police detained a woman yesterday to assist in investigations into an incident involving the harassment of visitors at a shopping mall in the capital.
Dang Wangi District Police Chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said police detained the 25-year-old woman at 5.40 pm in Bandar Sri Damansara.
