“The woman admitted to having been involved in the incident during initial investigations,” he said in a statement.
He urged members of the public with information about the incident to contact the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2146 0522 or 03-2146 0585, the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters Control Centre at 03-2600 2222, or visit the nearest police station.
A video circulated widely on social media on Sunday showing a woman and a man involved in an altercation after the woman was alleged to have mistreated a child at a shopping mall. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia ensures food, water and legal assistance for 130 citizens detained in Pakistan over cyber-scam links
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The government is monitoring the welfare of 130 Malaysians detained by Pakistani authorities over suspected links to a cyber-scam syndicate, ensuring that they have access to food, water and legal assistance.
Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni said Malaysian diplomatic representatives in every country were responsible for ensuring that Malaysians facing difficulties or detained by local authorities received appropriate attention, particularly in terms of their welfare and necessary assistance.
“So far, all 130 individuals who were arrested have been confirmed to be in good health. They have been provided with food and drinks, and we have also offered guidance on the legal avenues available to them,” he said.
He said this when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 and a motion on the ministry’s 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Lukanisman said that of the 130 individuals, 63 were from Sabah, 55 from Sarawak, five from Johor, three from Kuala Lumpur, two from Selangor, and one each from Penang and Kelantan.
Previously, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) confirmed that 130 Malaysians had been detained by Pakistani authorities in Rawalpindi over their alleged involvement in a cybercrime syndicate.
Yesterday, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Malaysia and Pakistan were discussing the coordination of follow-up actions concerning the detention of the Malaysians, who are suspected of involvement in online fraud activities in the country.
Meanwhile, Lukanisman said the government was in the final stages of preparing the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) card to register refugees under a module developed by Malaysia, in line with the government’s position that the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) should cease its refugee registration activities.
He said the transition needed to be carried out in an orderly manner, taking into account the large number of registration applications yet to be processed by the UNHCR, as well as the need to account for refugees already listed in the commission’s existing records.
“Our policy is for the UNHCR to halt all registration activities. However, we acknowledge that monitoring of its existing processes may not yet be sufficiently stringent as we are still in the process of finalising the implementation of the DPP to register refugees under the module introduced by the Malaysian government,” he said.
According to him, the DPP initiative demonstrated Malaysia’s ability to register refugees independently, although expanding the programme on a larger scale remained a challenge due to manpower constraints.
He said that from January until now, the government had managed to register only about 147 refugees because of the shortage of personnel to carry out the process.
Lukanisman said the government was also urging the UNHCR to expedite the resettlement of refugees to third countries, although the current volatile geopolitical situation had resulted in many countries tightening their borders and becoming less receptive to refugees.
The Dewan Rakyat subsequently passed the Foreign Ministry’s 2027 operating and development expenditure estimates, totalling RM1,212,144,700, by a majority voice vote following a debate involving 12 Members of Parliament.
The sitting will resume today. — Bernama

Title: As data centre power share heads for 21pc, Putrajaya moves to avoid ‘phantom demand’ hogging Malaysia’s grid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Data centre operators seeking grid connection in Peninsular Malaysia must now submit 10-year staggered energy projection plans and execute binding commercial pacts with Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), as the federal government clamps down on speculative developers hoarding power capacity.
The regulatory conditions were detailed in a written parliamentary reply by the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation to Rompin MP Datuk Abdul Khalib Abdullah, who questioned the mounting electricity and water footprints of hyperscale computing facilities on domestic reserve margins.
Under the framework, grid access approvals now hinge on strict technical evaluations assessing actual load matching and localized transmission capacity. Rather than granting bulk allocations upfront, the government is releasing grid access in phases governed by binding Electricity Supply Agreements (ESA) to eradicate what the ministry termed “phantom demand”, referring to artificial capacity bookings that inflate reserve commitments without translating into operational consumption.
Official data highlights a widening disconnect between contracted grid allocations and real-world utilization. As of August 2026, contracted data centre capacity stood at 2,346 megawatts (MW), yet active facilities were drawing only 1,374 MW, representing 58.6 per cent of contracted volumes.
The discrepancy leaves nearly 970 MW of generation capacity ring-fenced on paper but unused in practice, though the ministry did not distinguish between standard phased facility ramp-ups and purely speculative bookings.
The power clampdown arrives as data centres claim an increasingly dominant share of national energy production. Computing facilities are forecast to triple their electricity consumption from 7 per cent of peninsular demand (10,544 gigawatt-hours) in 2026 to 21 per cent (39,289 Gwh) by 2030.
The ministry gave assurances that this expansion has been integrated into the Peninsular Generation Development Plan, projecting that the regional reserve margin will remain stable between 25 and 27 per cent through 2035 through phased renewable additions, new thermal capacity, and operational life extensions for existing power plants.
To prevent hyperscalers from crowding out domestic consumers on the public grid, the government is urging operators to tap green power through Third Party Access (TPA) under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS), which allows direct corporate procurement from independent green power producers.
Operators developing mega-scale campuses are also being pushed to incorporate dedicated on-site power generation, including micro gas turbines and industrial rooftop solar installations, to alleviate pressure on national baseload margins.
While the Energy Commission continues to monitor load growth alongside the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry’s Data Centre Task Force, the ministerial reply leaves key regulatory enforcement rules unresolved.
The government stopped short of detailing financial penalties for operators whose real-world energy draw falls short of their 10-year projections, or establishing formal mechanisms to claw back and reallocate stranded capacity to competing industrial users.

Title: Yuneswaran: Deepavali expo boosts small traders while promoting racial unity through cultural celebrations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Large-scale business expos such as the 24th Deepavali Carnival (DC26) not only strengthen the economic prospects of local entrepreneurs and small traders, but also promote racial unity through cross-cultural integration.
Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said the Deepavali expo attracted people from diverse backgrounds, including visitors of different ethnicities and foreign tourists, who came together to celebrate Malaysia’s cultural diversity.
“The expo goes beyond business activities to include cultural programmes organised by the Indian community, helping to foster greater unity among the people.
“Unity encompasses all races, religions and cultures, and that is what makes Malaysia unique. I saw Indians, Malays and foreign visitors at the expo,” he said after visiting the event in Bukit Jalil here yestereday.
Yuneswaran said the expo gave new entrepreneurs a chance to expand their businesses without relying solely on government assistance, while complementing existing economic initiatives.
“This is not just about making profits; it also creates opportunities for small traders, entrepreneurs and those who are new to the business world,” he said.
The nine-day DC26, running from Oct 30 to Nov 7, features 450 booths showcasing Deepavali essentials and a wide selection of food, with free admission daily from noon to 10 pm. — Bernama

Title: Flooding shuts key Shah Alam expressway links, diversions active on NKVE and ELITE
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 4 — Pre-dawn flash floods forced the emergency closure of critical sections along the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) and the North-South Expressway Central Link (ELITE) near Shah Alam today, crippling morning peak-hour commutes across the central Klang Valley.
According to highway concessionaire PLUS Malaysia Bhd, all lanes at NKVE Km 9.1 between Shah Alam and Subang remained completely closed in both directions as of 9.04am.
To relieve mounting traffic queues, highway operators are diverting northbound traffic from Bukit Raja through the Setia Alam Toll Plaza, while southbound motorists from Subang are being channelled onto the ELITE highway.
Access from the Guthrie Corridor Expressway (GCE) towards the Shah Alam Toll Plaza also remained impassable this morning. However, traffic conditions saw partial relief after all lanes at the Shah Alam interchange along the ELITE highway, heading from Seafield towards Setia Alam, were reopened to traffic at 6.43am under cautious driving advisories.
The motorway disruptions began in the early hours following heavy overnight rain, with PLUS issuing its initial flood alert at 2.03am along the ELITE highway near the Shah Alam Toll Plaza. Water levels escalated rapidly by 2.30am as heavy surface runoff obstructed the entry ramp connecting the Guthrie Corridor Expressway, forcing the immediate closure of several entry and exit lanes.
Rising floodwaters subsequently breached NKVE Km 9.1 shortly before 2.40am, submerging the left and centre lanes between Shah Alam and Subang. By 3.00am, highway authorities enforced a total shutdown of the carriageway in both directions as the stretch became impassable to all vehicles, triggering emergency diversions towards Setia Alam and the Shah Alam interchange.
At 5.30am, localised ponding temporarily severed the ELITE interchange from Seafield before waters receded sufficiently to allow traffic through ahead of the peak morning rush.
With the mainline closure at NKVE Km 9.1 lingering through successive morning updates, PLUS advised road users to defer non-essential travel through the affected corridor, bypass the area using alternative state roads, and utilize live navigation applications to plan their journeys.

Title: Man slashed to death by three machete-wielding attackers in Teluk Intan, woman detained
Article:
TELUK INTAN, Nov 4 — A man died after being ambushed and slashed by three machete-wielding assailants outside a shop here yesterday afternoon, prompting police to arrest a 27-year-old local woman to assist in a murder investigation.
Hilir Perak district police headquarters dispatched officers to the scene after receiving an emergency 999 call from a member of the public at 3.53pm on Tuesday reporting a violent assault in progress in front of a shophouse.
The victim, who sustained catastrophic injuries in the attack, was rushed to Teluk Intan Hospital, where attending medical officers pronounced him dead in the emergency department.
Preliminary police investigations revealed that the victim was set upon by three unidentified men armed with machetes, who fled the area immediately following the attack. The motive behind the deadly assault remains under active investigation.
Detectives subsequently arrested the 27-year-old local woman to help establish the sequence of events leading up to the killing.
The case has been classified under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, alongside mandatory whipping of not less than 12 strokes upon conviction.
Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said in a statement today that investigators are appealing for eyewitnesses who observed the incident, or anyone who spotted suspicious individuals and vehicles near the scene around the time of the assault.
Members of the public with relevant information are urged to contact the Hilir Perak district police headquarters at 05-629 9222 or visit the nearest police station.
Chua also urged the community to refrain from circulating unverified claims on social media, warning that online speculation could compromise ongoing investigative work.

Title: Anwar moved by 1982 photograph showing late supporter celebrating his first election victory
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was deeply moved upon receiving an old photograph from a student from Alor Setar, Kedah, which captured him celebrating his first electoral victory for the Permatang Pauh parliamentary seat in 1982.
In a Facebook post, the Prime Minister shared that the photograph was presented by Zahra Mohamad Zelman, who approached him accompanied by her friends from Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Sultanah Asma at the Parliament building yesterday.
Anwar noted that the image captured a moment when he was being celebrated by Zahra’s great-grandfather, the late Arshad Ahmad, following his win in the Permatang Pauh constituency.
“A single photograph, yet it holds so much memory and stories. It evokes the time which has long since passed, but the remembrance of the individuals who were once present who became part of this long journey of struggle remains etched deep within my heart,” he wrote in the post.
During the encounter, Anwar encouraged Zahra and her friends to continue their pursuit of knowledge, to have the courage to harbour and pursue their aspirations, and to never cease in their efforts. He also offered prayers that their life journeys would always be made smooth. — Bernama

Title: PTPTN first class honours loan exemption under review as govt weighs fairness and sustainability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 —The government will study a loan repayment exemption policy for previous National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers who earned first-class honours degrees.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the review would consider fairness to borrowers while ensuring the country’s education financing policy remains sustainable.
“We will continue to review PTPTN’s policy to ensure that assistance is targeted and provided only to those who genuinely need it. Any exemptions will also be assessed in line with this policy,” he said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) for the Finance Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday
Chong Chieng Jen (PH-Stampin) interjected to highlight concerns among borrowers who took out PTPTN loans in 2025 or earlier, saying changes to the eligibility requirements breached their contracts.
Chong said previous loan agreements explicitly provided for repayment exemptions for borrowers who graduated with first-class honours degrees, and urged the government to maintain the exemption for existing borrowers until a new policy is announced.
On measures to support graduates, Amir Hamzah said the government allows PTPTN borrowers earning up to RM2,500 a month to defer repayments, while those earning between RM2,501 and RM3,000 must pay a minimum of RM50 monthly to ease their transition into the workforce.
He said borrowers who make regular repayments without falling into arrears are eligible for a 10 per cent discount, while employers who help repay their employees’ loans will qualify for tax deductions from Jan 1, 2027, to Dec 31, 2028.
In a separate development, Amir Hamzah said the government, through Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), would review insurance providers’ operating procedures after complaints that policyholders at private hospitals faced restrictions on their choice of specialist doctors.
He said the government would discuss the matter with BNM to protect consumer rights and curb rising medical costs.
“Regulation of the insurance industry falls under BNM, and as part of this initiative, the central bank will review the procedures adopted by insurance providers.
“Equally important is ensuring that all industry players comply with sound regulations to prevent medical cost inflation from rising, as everyone would ultimately bear the resulting costs,” he said.
On expanding access to comprehensive healthcare protection, Amir Hamzah said the affordable MediAsas insurance and takaful product is expected to be launched in late January next year, adding that the product will use a diagnosis-based payment system to curb rising treatment costs, while allowing Employees Provident Fund (EPF) members under 55 to pay premiums using their Akaun Sejahtera.
As part of efforts to support workers’ welfare, the government has agreed to provide employers of small and medium enterprises with fewer than 75 employees a first-year premium subsidy of RM200 per worker, with each company eligible for a maximum of 50 workers, he added.
The Dewan Rakyat subsequently approved the Finance Ministry’s estimated 2027 operating and development expenditure of RM68,159,895,600 under Budget 2027 by a voice vote, following debate by 27 MPs. — Bernama

Title: Sabah Pakatan chief condemns use of religious sentiment in political debate over parliamentary agreement
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 4 — Sabah Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud has reminded political parties not to exploit religious sentiment as a weapon to challenge opponents’ strategies, following remarks linking parliamentary democracy as an institution to an end-times figure.
The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) expressed regret over a statement by PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang, who was alleged to have likened the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) approach to “Dajjal” (literally the Deceitful Messiah), stressing that such a label was highly unfamiliar and could confuse Muslims in Sabah.
“When political arguments are no longer sufficient, must end-times terminology be turned into a weapon? The CSA can be debated rationally within the framework of parliamentary democracy without resorting to religious sentiment to discredit those with differing views,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He noted that the CSA approach had previously been adopted when PAS was part of the federal government, raising questions about the rationale for labelling the mechanism negatively.
Mustapha said diversity in religion, ethnicity and cultural backgrounds had long been central to uniting Sabah’s multiracial society and should not be used to fuel animosity.
“For Sabahans, portraying fellow Muslims in such a negative light merely because they hold different political views is alien and unacceptable.
“Religion should unite, not divide, and Sabah does not need to be lectured on unity by those who continue to label one another,” he said.
He therefore called on all Sabahans to uphold the harmony they have long enjoyed and strongly reject divisive political practices that exploit religion for power, while urging all parties to find common ground in safeguarding the people’s well-being. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: National security, UUCA repeal and misleading ‘badal haj’ ads among key issues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Issues concerning national security amid rising military tensions in the Asia-Pacific region, the future governance of universities following the repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) and efforts to tackle misleading advertisements for
badal haj
services are among the matters to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official website, William Leong Jee Keen (PH-Selayang) will ask the Defence Minister during the Questions for Oral Answers session about the government’s stance on rising tensions and military escalation in the Asia-Pacific region, particularly measures to safeguard national security and maintain stability within Asean.
Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob (BN-Bera) will seek clarification from the Higher Education Minister on how the government will ensure that the repeal of UUCAdoes not create legislative gaps or uncertainty in university administration, as well as the key principles underpinning the proposed One Higher Education Act.
Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai) will ask the Prime Minister to outline the government’s mechanisms for conducting preliminary checks on advertisers’ identities, company status, licences, payment recipient accounts and the validity of claims concerning the performance of badal haj before such advertisements are promoted to the public.
Aminolhuda Hassan (PH-Sri Gading) will also ask the Prime Minister to identify the remaining 25 per cent of recommendations made by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Tabung Haji that have yet to be implemented, as well as the target timeframe and action plan to ensure their full implementation.
Following the Questions for Oral Answers session, the Dewan Rakyat will resume the committee-stage debate and ministerial replies on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar, the Committee Stage debate on the 2027 Budget runs from Nov 2 to 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting runs for 37 days until Dec 8. — Bernama

Title: Save your tears (for the traffic): 130,000 The Weeknd fans set to gridlock Bukit Jalil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Motorists and commuters heading towards Bukit Jalil face severe traffic gridlock this evening and tomorrow as Canadian superstar The Weeknd takes the stage at the National Stadium for the two-night finale of his global tour.
With roughly 130,000 concertgoers expected across both nights at the 80,000-capacity arena, traffic authorities have issued advisories warning of heavy delays across major highway arteries feeding into KL Sports City.
Routes to avoid
Bottlenecks are anticipated along the Shah Alam Expressway (KESAS), the Maju Expressway (MEX), the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway, the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2), and local arterial access roads.
Drivers are told to adhere strictly to the instructions of on-site marshals and stay alert for high pedestrian foot traffic around the stadium precinct.
Motorists are specifically advised to avoid Jalan Merah Caga and Jalan Barat, where congestion is expected to peak.
Instead, incoming drivers should stay on the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway, exit at the Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) junction, and follow navigational signage towards designated parking zones.
Park here instead?
To relieve parking pressure around the immediate stadium perimeter, alternative parking has been set up at MRANTI Park and the Calvary Convention Centre.
Concertgoers relying on e-hailing services must use the dedicated pick-up and drop-off facility established at the Endah Parade E-Hailing Hub to prevent curb-side drop-offs from choking stadium access routes.
Better yet, take the train
Public transport operator Rapid KL has extended operating hours across selected train lines on both nights to encourage fans to leave their cars behind. The final boarding cut-off at the Bukit Jalil LRT station on the Sri Petaling Line is set at 12.30am for direct services bound for both Putra Heights and Sentul Timur.
Passengers requiring rail transfers must board at Bukit Jalil significantly earlier to secure connections. Commuters transferring to the LRT Ampang Line or the MRT Putrajaya Line must depart Bukit Jalil by midnight. This allows Ampang Line riders to catch the 12.13am final connection at Chan Sow Lin, while Putrajaya Line commuters can change trains at Sungai Besi before the last services depart for Kwasa Damansara at 12.15am and Putrajaya Sentral at 12.34am.
An earlier 11.30pm departure deadline applies to fans heading towards the LRT Kelana Jaya Line, the KL Monorail, or the MRT Kajang Line. Passengers transferring to the Kelana Jaya Line at Masjid Jamek can catch the final train to Putra Heights at 12.03am or Gombak at 12.17am, while monorail riders at Hang Tuah have until 12.08am for Titiwangsa and 12.10am for KL Sentral. Commuters bound for the MRT Kajang Line face a two-step transit journey: they must transfer to the Putrajaya Line at Sungai Besi by 11.45pm, then complete a second transfer at Tun Razak Exchange (TRX) before final departures at 12.10am towards Kwasa Damansara and 12.13am towards Kajang.
To support transit use, Rapid KL highlighted 15 park-and-ride hubs along the LRT Ampang and Sri Petaling corridors, including facilities at Ampang, Pandan Jaya, Taman Perindustrian Puchong, Kinrara BK5, Sentul, Putra Heights, and Sungai Besi. Another 14 multi-storey car parks are available along the MRT Putrajaya Line, serving stations such as Metro Prima, Sri Damansara Timur, Cyberjaya Utara, UPM, and Taman Naga Emas.
Drivers using official rail-operated parking pay flat daily rates ranging between RM4.30 and RM5.00 per entry, provided they tap in and out using the identical Touch ‘n Go card utilized for their train journey. Parking bay occupancy can be tracked in real time via the MyRapid Pulse mobile application.
The two Bukit Jalil dates bring the curtain down on The Weeknd’s After Hours Til Dawn tour, which etched its name in modern pop history by selling more than 7.5 million tickets and generating over US$1 billion (RM4.1 billion) in box-office receipts, making it the highest-earning concert tour ever mounted by a male solo artist.

Title: Working or retired? Here is what Budget 2027 offers Malaysians over 60
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Reaching 60 does not automatically mean clocking out for good, drawing a pension, or qualifying for welfare. Depending on your circumstances, Budget 2027 packs a variety of measures that impact older Malaysians differently.
Whether you are still in the workforce, managing your retirement, or navigating the rising costs of elder care, the latest federal Budget has something for you.
Here is a breakdown of what Malaysians aged 60 and above stand to gain.
Cash aid through STR and SARA
Budget 2027 increases the combined allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to a massive RM16 billion.
SARA assistance of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 a year, will now reach all eligible STR recipients, benefiting up to nine million Malaysians.
Separately, the government will extend a special SARA Madani assistance of RM100, paid twice a year, to eligible adults who do not qualify for STR. Expect these payouts just before Hari Raya Aidilfitri and the 70th Merdeka celebrations, giving recipients a handy RM200 boost.
Higher individual income tax relief and lower rates
For older Malaysians still earning an income, the government plans to increase individual income tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000 starting from Year of Assessment 2027. Naturally, this only benefits those with taxable income.
The Budget also cuts one percentage point off individual income tax rates for specific brackets. Chargeable income between RM70,001 and RM100,000 drops from 19 per cent to 18 per cent. Meanwhile, the RM100,001 to RM150,000 tier falls from 25 per cent to 24 per cent.
Put together, these tweaks will leave up to RM1,600 in extra disposable income for roughly five million taxpayers.
Flexible EPF withdrawals under i-Emas
Retirees looking to stretch their savings can tap into the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) i-Emas scheme.
This facility allows members reaching 55 and 60 to opt for monthly withdrawals, letting their remaining balance continue compounding with annual dividends.
Through the scheme, you can schedule monthly payouts of at least RM100 for a minimum of 12 months.
Alternatively, members can mix monthly payments with partial withdrawals instead of cashing out their entire eligible savings in one go.
Expanded tax relief for aged care expenses
Caring for ageing parents and grandparents will get slightly easier on the wallet. From Year of Assessment 2027, tax relief for their care will expand beyond strict healthcare costs to cover all types of care expenses, including home care, day-care, and residential centres.
The existing RM8,000 claim limit remains intact. Crucially, however, you no longer need a registered medical practitioner to verify these claims.
Taxpayers simply need to provide receipts alongside a written declaration from the carer or a copy of the carer's work permit.
Lower service tax for care centres
Starting Jan 1, 2027, the service tax rate on elderly care services drops from 8 per cent to 6 per cent.
Taking it a step further, the government will completely exempt qualifying elderly care centres from service tax if their annual fees fall below RM96,000 per person.
These centres must be registered under the Care Centres Act 1993 or the Private Aged Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 2018. Any fees exceeding the RM96,000 threshold will attract the reduced 6 per cent rate.
RM1.3 billion for older Malaysians’ welfare
The government is setting aside RM1.3 billion in 2027 to assist nearly 200,000 older Malaysians. Currently, the Social Welfare Department runs the Bantuan Warga Emas (BWE) programme, which provides eligible older Malaysians with RM600 a month.
While the Budget does not explicitly raise this individual monthly payout, the massive RM1.3 billion allocation ensures the continuation of this vital safety net for those meeting the strict citizenship, residency, and financial criteria.
Pension bumps and bonuses for government retirees
Civil service veterans will have plenty to smile about. The minimum monthly pension will jump from RM1,000 to RM1,350, directly benefiting nearly 59,000 pensioners, Armed Forces veterans, and derivative pension recipients.
On top of that, over one million government retirees will receive a special financial assistance payout of RM750.
The government will split this bonus into two instalments, paying out just before Hari Raya Aidilfitri and the 70th Merdeka anniversary.
Faster bankruptcy relief for caregivers
Financial distress can hit families hard, especially those managing heavy caregiving duties. Starting in 2027, the Second Chance Fast Track Policy will expand to include primary caregivers of family members who are aged 60 and above, disabled, or chronically ill.
While not a direct cash handout, this policy expedites bankruptcy relief, offering a critical lifeline to caregivers drowning in debt.
New laws to protect older Malaysians
Looking at the bigger picture of Malaysia's ageing population, the government plans to draft a new bill to address elderly abandonment and fortify the national care system.
This is a pre-emptive legislative move rather than an immediate financial benefit, signalling a stronger legal framework to protect the welfare of older Malaysians in the years to come.

Title: Private universities steal the spotlight as Malaysia sets a historic record in QS Asia 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — More than 50 Malaysian universities penetrated the QS World University Rankings Asia 2027 for the first time, with 11 emerging among the top 100 in Asia.
Overall, Malaysia is the eighth most represented higher education system in Asia, with 55 featured universities on the list. The country also stands on par with Japan and Korea with eight entries in the top 50.
Of the 16 Malaysian universities that achieved record-high positions for 2027, 12 were private universities.
They include Sunway University, INTI International University, Asia Pacific University of Technology and Innovation (APU), SEGi University, IMU University, MILA University, Tunku Abdul Rahman University of Management and Technology, Perdana University, Quest International University (QIU), Nilai University, UNITAR International University and Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah (UniSHAMS).
The highest-ranked private university was Taylor’s University at the 32nd spot, albeit dropping five spots from the previous edition.
Sunway University also ranked among the top 50 for the first time while INTI International University made it into the top 100 for the first time.
Universiti Malaya (UM) remained the country’s best-performing university, emerging among the top 20 universities in Asia for the ninth consecutive year despite slipping two spots to the 17th rank this edition.
Meanwhile, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) entered the top 20 for the first time, rising four spots from the previous edition while Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) emerged top in Asia for the Faculty with PhD indicator.
260,000 international students by 2030
QS senior vice-president Ben Sowter said Malaysia has more than doubled the number of universities in the top 100 in the QS World University Rankings: Asia in the last decade. The number of universities in the top 50 has also increased from only two in 2017 to eight in 2027.
“Its renown as an education hub in Southeast Asia is only growing, and research from QS suggests that, by the end of the decade, international student numbers are projected to reach about 260,000,” Sowter said.
According to the 2027 edition, Malaysia has the most well-represented higher education system in two key indicators. It has 24 universities in the top 100 entries for the International Faculty indicator and 31 in the top 100 entries in the International Students indicator.
However, it only has one entry in the top 100 for Citations per Paper and Papers per Faculty indicators.
How did other countries perform?
The QS Asia University Rankings 2027 evaluated 1722 universities across 26 locations.
The University of Hong Kong retained the top spot in the ranking while Peking University and Tsinghua University from China finished second and third respectively.
Hong Kong also recorded the highest number of universities in the top 10 while Japan logged one of Asia’s highest drop rates.
Meanwhile, Singapore’s two universities also dropped out of the top five, with the National University of Singapore (NUS) now ranking sixth in Asia while the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) Singapore settled at the eighth position.
Maldives also debuted this edition, featuring The Maldives National University and Villa College.

Title: Hafidz Othman appointed new Prisons Department chief, takes office on Nov 5
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — Deputy Commissioner General of Prisons (Community) Hafidz Othman has been appointed the new Commissioner General of Prisons, effective Nov 5, the Prisons Department said.
In a statement today, the department said Hafidz received his appointment letter from Public Service director-general Tan Sri Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz.
He will succeed Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Razak, who has held the post since Feb 14, 2025.
Hafidz, who holds a Bachelor of Laws degree from Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), began his career as a prison officer with the rank of Deputy Superintendent at Miri Prison in Sarawak.
During his 32 years of service, he has held several key positions, including heading Seremban Prison, Negeri Sembilan Prisons, the International Affairs and Prisoner Transfer Division, and the Correctional Division, according to the statement.
He also served as Deputy Commissioner General of Prisons (Management) in 2025.
The department expressed hope that Hafidz would draw on his experience, expertise and leadership to further strengthen its correctional services, in line with the aspirations of Malaysia Madani and the Public Service Reform Agenda. — Bernama

Title: Govt pays RM20.27b in income tax refunds to 3.65m taxpayer cases as at Oct 31
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — A total of RM20.271 billion in income tax refunds involving 3.65 million taxpayer cases had been paid as at Oct 31, 2026.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said of the total, RM6.84 billion had been refunded to 3.4 million individual taxpayers, while RM13.036 billion had been refunded to 206,234 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
“In carrying out the refunds, the government prioritises excess tax refunds to individuals as well as MSMEs,” he said during the winding-up session of the Supply Bill at the committee stage for the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Amir Hamzah also said that, in line with this approach, the number of taxpayers with excess tax credits had been reduced by almost half to about 550,000 as at Oct 31, 2026, compared with more than one million as at Dec 31, 2025.
“The government is also committed to ensuring that outstanding tax refunds are fully settled promptly, as part of efforts to improve tax administration efficiency and safeguard taxpayers’ rights, in line with the Madani government’s fiscal reform agenda,” he said in response to questions raised by Members of Parliament (MPs) for Bachok, Klang and Pendang.
Amir Hamzah reiterated the government’s commitment to addressing the backlog of excess income tax refunds to ensure that all outstanding payments are made promptly.
A total of 27 MPs took part in the committee-stage debate on the MoF.
He said the views and feedback raised would help the government review how each allocation was managed and implemented for the benefit of the people.
Overall, the 2027 operating supply expenditure allocation for the ministry increased to RM68.16 billion, compared with the revised allocation of RM61.5 billion for this year.
He said the increase reflected the Madani government’s commitment to easing the cost of living and ensuring the well-being of the people. — Bernama

Title: Johor identifies 337 flood hotspots as state braces for northeast monsoon
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Nov 3 — The Johor government will focus on 337 flood hotspots statewide as the northeast monsoon is expected to affect the state from this month until January next year.
State Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said priority would be given to areas with high population density and a history of major flooding, including the districts of Kota Tinggi, Batu Pahat and Segamat.
“Based on updates from the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), 35 flood hotspots, including new additions, have been identified.
“The Public Works Department (JKR) has also identified 30 high-risk road locations that comprise 21 sites on federal roads and nine on state roads,” he told reporters after a working visit to the Sungai Rinting flood wall project here today.
Also present were Permas assemblyman Baharudin Mohamed Taib and senior government agency officials.
Mohamad Fazli said the measures outlined included hotspot mapping, drain maintenance, cleaning and dredging drainage systems, ensuring machinery was ready, public outreach and the use of the eBencana (electronic disaster) reporting system.
He said the relevant projects included Phase 1 of the Sungai Johor Flood Mitigation Plan, the Sungai Pemandi Flood Mitigation Plan and a flood alleviation project in Kampung Sungai Kapal Lama in Pengerang.
In Batu Pahat, Mohamad Fazli said the DID had identified 41 flood hotspots, while the JKR had detected 21 high-risk locations along federal and state roads, covering a total distance of 6.5 kilometres.
He added that preparations would include road pavement maintenance works worth RM11.79 million, non-pavement works worth RM3.20 million and an allocation of RM1.92 million under the Malaysian Road Records Information System (MARRIS) for drainage-related works.
“Alternative route plans via the FT024 federal road and the PLUS Highway have also been planned.
“Mobile pumps at the Parit Botak sluice gate, flood mitigation projects – such as the Bandar Batu Pahat and Sungai Batu Pahat flood mitigation schemes – as well as coastal embankment upgrading works, are also being given due attention,” he said.
In Segamat, Mohamad Fazli said the DID had identified 29 flood hotspots, while the JKR had identified 16 high-risk locations, comprising eight federal roads and eight state roads.
“Efforts are also focused on monitoring river levels and roadways, as well as coordinating with the Batu Pahat district, which is located downstream,” he said.
In Muar, he said 65 flood hotspots had been identified, the highest number among the districts listed by the DID.
In Tangkak, 26 hotspots had been identified, with priority measures including inspecting culverts and drainage systems, monitoring roadways and coordinating maintenance efforts among the relevant agencies.
Mohamad Fazli said there were also 44 flood hotspots in Johor Bahru, 29 in Kluang, 19 in Pontian, 27 in Kulai and 22 in Mersing.
In a related development, he said the state government was preparing an application for an emergency allocation of between RM20 million and RM30 million to carry out maintenance works and flood preparedness measures in high-risk areas throughout November and December.
“Priority will be given to tasks that can be executed immediately, specifically maintenance work, whereas large-scale projects, such as the construction of embankments and flood-retaining walls, will require a longer timeframe,” he added.

Title: After Customs flags import irregularities, maritime expert asks MACC to revisit RM220m crude cargo report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — A maritime industry executive today asked whether the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) would take further action on his report over alleged discrepancies in petroleum cargo records, following the Royal Malaysian Customs Department’s latest disclosure on import declaration irregularities.
Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan lodged the report on June 5 over alleged discrepancies between bills of lading and the physical movement of petroleum cargo at Tanjung Langsat Port, Johor, in transactions reportedly worth millions of ringgit.
The report involved two petroleum cargoes totalling 76,954.325 metric tonnes of Atlanta Crude, valued at more than RM220 million, which were discharged at Tanjung Langsat.
Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the maritime industry, questioned whether the latest information from Customs could give MACC grounds to revisit the concerns raised in his report.
Customs director-general Datuk Seri Amran Ahmad was quoted by
Harian Metro
as saying that certain importers had allegedly manipulated documents, under-declared the value, weight and quantity of imported goods, and used incorrect tariff codes to evade or reduce import duties and taxes.
Amran said this could potentially result in millions of ringgit in revenue losses to the government.
Jeyenderan said the key concern was traceability, particularly how the authorities and relevant parties could establish what happened to the cargo after it entered storage tanks containing existing inventory, including any subsequent movement, mixing or blending.
He said the relevant records should show the quantity discharged into each tank, the existing inventory, subsequent product movements, laboratory specifications and the quantities eventually removed or transferred, to ensure an unbroken documentary trail.
He stressed that Maritime Network had acted only as the vessel or shipping agent for the cargo movements, and was not the cargo owner, terminal operator, laboratory or Customs authority.
As such, he said, the roles and responsibilities of all parties involved must be clearly established.
Jeyenderan wants MACC to clarify whether the Customs disclosure warrants further investigation, particularly regarding the accuracy of cargo declarations and the applicable regulatory treatment.
He said the main concern was whether the cargo declarations, supporting documents and actual physical movement of the petroleum products were consistent with the relevant Customs requirements.
He also called on the authorities to clarify whether there were any regulatory or revenue implications arising from the handling of petroleum cargoes, particularly where shared storage tanks and blending arrangements were involved.

Title: New law replacing AUKU will not curtail students’ freedom of expression, says Zahid
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 3 — The new Bill to replace the now-repealed Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) will not affect students’ freedom of expression, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said the Cabinet agreed that the proposed legislation would be limited to matters concerning university administration, including academic affairs, governance and the appointment of senate members,
Ahmad Zahid also said that the new law would also cover the selection of university management personnel, including vice-chancellors and deputy vice-chancellors.
“The new legislation, which will carry a different name, will no longer include the seven provisions concerning students, including those on freedom, under AUKU, which restricted their freedom to engage in activities,” he said.
He was asked about the latest developments in the proposal for a new law to replace AUKU after attending the Apa Khabar Mahasiswa: Patriotisme Diperkasa programme at Universiti Teknologi Mara’s (UiTM) Alor Gajah Campus in Melaka today.
Also present at the event was Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir.
Ahmad Zahid, also the Rural and Regional Development Minister, said universities should not penalise students for expressing their opinions unless their remarks involved sensitive issues relating to race, religion and the royal institution (3R).
“Under AUKU, universities did take action against students. Now that the Act has been repealed, students remain subject to existing laws, including criminal legislation.
“...if students are simply expressing differing opinions, political beliefs or the views of young people, I believe universities should welcome this rather than take legal action against them, unless their actions breach the law,” he said.
In a separate development, Ahmad Zahid said enrolment for the Department of Quantum Technology at UiTM was expected to begin next semester under a training-for-trainers concept.
“Initially, the academic staff will be sent for master’s or PhD studies, or short courses, to equip those with backgrounds in information technology and digital technology to lead the department before it is upgraded to the Faculty of Quantum Technology,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid announced earlier in October that RM500,000 would be allocated as initial funding to establish UiTM’s Department of Quantum Technology. — Bernama

Title: Govt approves over RM250m for ECRL expansion plans and new Kota Bharu bus terminal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — The Madani government has approved more than RM250 million to strengthen the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) development in Kelantan, according to the Ministry of Finance (MOF).
This includes building a new bus terminal at the Kota Bharu ECRL Station and preliminary works for a proposed extension to Rantau Panjang, said the ministry in a statement today.
Of the total, RM30 million has been allocated for the new bus terminal, while more than RM200 million will fund preliminary works for the proposed ECRL extension from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang.
“The preliminary works include initial design, land surveys and investigations, an environmental impact assessment (EIA), preparation of the Railway Scheme and site preparation works to facilitate the project’s implementation in the next phase,” it said.
The investment aims to enhance transport infrastructure and create opportunities for competitive economic development in Kelantan. The development is expected to spur business activities, strengthen the logistics sector, attract investment and create job opportunities for the local population, said MOF.
The ministry emphasised that national development must be inclusive and balanced to ensure that the benefits of progress reach people throughout the country, including in Kelantan, rather than being concentrated solely in major cities. — Bernama

Title: Fashion Valet trial: Investment funds cannot be used to pay dividends, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Sessions Court hearing the case involving Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd (Fashion Valet) founders Datin Vivy Sofinas Yusof and her husband, Datuk Fadzarudin Shah Anuar, was told today that investment funds could not be used to pay dividends to any party, including the company’s shareholders.
Corporate lawyer Anne Wong Wai Yee, 49, who was involved in drafting the shareholders’ agreement between the couple and seven other companies, including Fashion Valet, on March 5, 2018, said the agreement did not contain any provision allowing investment funds to be used for such payments.
The other six companies were Proven Holding Sdn Bhd, MY E.G. Capital Sdn Bhd, Transasia E-Commerce Inc., Start Today Co. Ltd., Reussi Sdn Bhd and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd.
“The declaration of dividends requires the approval of a majority of the directors, including those appointed by Start Today Co. Ltd. and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd,” she testified during the trial of the couple, who are facing charges of criminal breach of trust involving RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah Nasional Berhad (Khazanah) and Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB).
The sixth prosecution witness said the agreement also specified the permitted uses of the investment funds, namely expenditure on technology development, stores and warehouses, as well as products and brands.
“The permitted allocation of the investment funds was as follows: 30 per cent for consumer acquisition, 30 per cent for technology development, 20 per cent for store and warehouse expansion, and 20 per cent for product and brand acquisition, based on the total investment value.
“Typically, such expenditures require approval from a majority of the board of directors,” Wong said.
She said Fashion Valet was required to submit summaries of the utilisation of the investment funds to the board of directors on a quarterly and annual basis until the entire amount had been utilised.
“However, I have no knowledge of the distribution of dividends or the transfer of investment funds received by Fashion Valet, as my scope of work was limited to drafting and coordinating the contractual agreements.
“The subsequent execution of these agreements by the parties involved falls outside the scope of my professional duties,” said Wong, a partner at Karen Kaur & Anne Wong Partnership.
She further testified that Fashion Valet was prohibited from extending loans or credit to its directors, shareholders, related companies or any other parties without the approval of a majority of the board of directors.
“Furthermore, Fashion Valet is restricted from entering into any agreement or understanding with parties related to the company, its directors or shareholders, involving RM50,000 or more annually, without the approval of a majority of the directors, including those appointed by Start Today Co. Ltd. and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd,” she added.
Referring to a Subscription Agreement dated June 4, 2018, Wong said the document constituted a binding agreement between the relevant parties, namely Fashion Valet, Proven Holdings and PNB, concerning PNB’s investment in the company.
“Essentially, this agreement sets out the terms and conditions of PNB’s investment in Fashion Valet, whereby, in exchange for the investment, Fashion Valet would issue Redeemable Convertible Preference Shares (RCPS) to PNB,” she testified.
Vivy, 38, and Fadzarudin, 37, are charged with criminal breach of trust, allegedly committed with common intention in their capacity as directors of Fashion Valet, involving RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB.
The charge alleges that they had authorised payments totalling RM8 million from Fashion Valet’s corporate bank account to a company known as 30 Maple without the approval of the company’s board of directors.
The alleged offence took place at the Public Bank Berhad branch in Bukit Damansara, at 36-40 Medan Setia 2, Plaza Damansara, Bukit Damansara, on Aug 21, 2018.
The charge, under Section 409 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, provides for imprisonment of between two and 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
The couple also pleaded not guilty to an alternative charge of dishonestly misappropriating, with common intention, property belonging to Fashion Valet, namely RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB, at the same location and on the same date.
The alternative charge, under Section 403 of the Penal Code, carries a penalty of imprisonment of between six months and five years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
The trial, before Judge Rosli Ahmad, continues on Nov 20. — Bernama

Title: Traders risk RM100,000 fine for hidden charges, Parliament told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Traders who impose hidden charges or disclose additional fees only at the final stage of a transaction may face legal action, including fines of up to RM100,000, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the practice misled consumers and undermined their right to know the actual price before making a purchase.
“This means consumers should have clear information on the amount they need to pay, rather than discovering certain charges at the final stage of a transaction,” he said in a written reply in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Muhammad Islahuddin Abas (PN-Mersing) on measures taken by the ministry to curb the practice of imposing additional or hidden charges disclosed only at the final stage of a transaction, resulting in the actual price exceeding the displayed or advertised price, particularly in the services, food and beverage, and online transaction sectors.
Armizan said Section 10B(1) of the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011 [Act 723] allows action against businesses that fail to include all taxes, duties, and other charges in the prices of goods or services they display, advertise, publish, or quote.
The same Act stipulates under Section 57 that corporate bodies found in breach of the provision may be fined up to RM100,000, while individuals face penalties of up to RM50,000 in fines, two years’ imprisonment, or both.
He said the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) also had enforcement powers under the Consumer Protection Act 1999 [Act 599], particularly Section 12(1)(a), which makes misleading representations about the price of goods or services an offence.
Section 12(3)(c) of the Act further stipulates that a price display is considered misleading if it gives the impression that the stated price covers everything, when additional charges are in fact imposed separately.
“Sections 9 and 10 of the Act also prohibit false or misleading claims about the nature and characteristics of goods or services. The provisions cover both transactions at physical business premises and online transactions.
“Those found in breach of the relevant provisions may be penalised under Section 145 of Act 599. The penalty for corporate bodies is a fine of up to RM100,000, while individuals may be fined up to RM50,000, jailed for up to three years, or both,” he said.
Armizan said KPDN had introduced guidelines on the All-Inclusive Pricing Policy to promote price transparency, particularly in the food and beverage, e-commerce and delivery sectors, requiring consumers to be informed of the total price, including the base price, service charges and delivery fees, before confirming an order.
He said the ministry also enforced the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering (Price Marking of Goods and Charges for Services) Order 2020, which requires service providers and business premises to display clearly and prominently a list of services offered and the charges imposed.
“The ministry will continue to step up monitoring and enforcement to ensure traders comply with price disclosure requirements, and urges consumers to check the final price before making payment.
“Consumers should also report to KPDN any instances of hidden fees or discrepancies between advertised prices and the actual amounts charged,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Mount Kinabalu training centre faces calls to halt work over indigenous, environmental concerns
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 3 — The ongoing construction of a high-altitude training centre on Mount Kinabalu has come under scrutiny, with indigenous groups and tourism stakeholders questioning its environmental impact, approvals and whether communities with customary ties to the mountain were adequately consulted.
The controversy surfaced around October 30 after photographs showing structures and apparent drilling activities near Sayat-Sayat circulated on social media, prompting calls for authorities to clarify the nature and purpose of the work.
The photographs prompted criticism over a lack of transparency, including from Kundasang Tourism and Culture Association chairman Datuk Japiril Suhaimin, who called for an investigation into the project's location, scope and approvals, as well as its potential effects on water sources, soil stability and biodiversity.
Bundu Tuhan Village Heritage and Culture head Adrian Soros also questioned whether communities with customary ties to the mountain had been consulted, saying many villagers were unaware of the construction.
He raised concerns about drilling into the mountain, which he said went against customary beliefs, as well as the protection of local water sources and the management of human waste at high altitude.
Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin subsequently issued a statement saying the project was not new and had originally been proposed under the Kinabalu Park Development Plan in 2015.
He said the project had obtained approval from the Sabah Parks Board of Trustees and endorsement from the Mount Kinabalu Native Customary Advisory Council.
“The HATC was originally proposed under the Kinabalu Park Development Plan in 2015, but its implementation was deferred following the earthquake that struck Mount Kinabalu that year.
“The initiative was subsequently revived and officially launched in 2025 as part of Sabah’s efforts to diversify its tourism offerings and strengthen its position as an internationally recognised mountaineering destination,” he said.
The new development would provide basic accommodation and specialised facilities to support high-altitude training and mountaineering activities.
Jafry said the centre was intended to cater to mountaineers preparing for expeditions to higher-altitude destinations, including Mount Kilimanjaro, Aconcagua and Mount Everest, by providing facilities for altitude acclimatisation, technical training and familiarisation with specialised climbing equipment.
He said construction involved lightweight, prefabricated and modular building materials to minimise environmental disturbance, with the structures designed to withstand strong winds and challenging weather conditions at higher elevations.
The construction method also avoided the use of heavy machinery in view of the mountain’s sensitive natural environment.
Jafry said the project’s approval and implementation must respect Mount Kinabalu’s cultural and spiritual significance to indigenous communities, as reflected in the involvement of the Native Customary Advisory Council.
The minister nevertheless emphasised that the approval did not exempt the project from complying with stipulated conditions, technical specifications and environmental regulations.
“We take the concerns raised by the public seriously. The ministry will consider a comprehensive investigation to ascertain whether all approved specifications, environmental safeguards and regulatory conditions have been fully observed.
“Should any non-compliance be established, the ministry will not hesitate to pursue the necessary enforcement measures in accordance with the law,” he said.
However, despite his statement, the Dayak International Organisation (DIO) today called for all construction, drilling and installation work at the site to stop, alleging that the development violated indigenous customary law protected under the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP).
Its United Nations representative, Datuk Petinggi Andrew Ambrose Atama Katama, questioned the use of the Mount Kinabalu Native Customary Advisory Council to endorse the project, saying this did not replace the need for consent from communities, particularly the Kadazandusun and Momogun.
Andrew described Aki Nabalu as a sacred living entity and ancestral repository rather than a commercial asset for generating state revenue.
DIO also called for an independent environmental audit, including an assessment of wastewater impact on local water catchments, and said it would raise the matter at the United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues and the Unesco Global Geoparks Network.
Mount Kinabalu, also known as Aki Nabalu, is Sabah's highest peak at 4,095 metres and holds deep cultural and spiritual significance for indigenous communities, particularly the Kadazandusun.
Every year, locals hold sacred rituals to honour the mountain spirits, seek permission and protection, and ensure the safety and well-being of climbers.
Kinabalu Park was inscribed as a Unesco World Heritage Site in 2000 for its exceptional biodiversity, including thousands of plant species and a wide range of habitats.

Title: Zahid denies trying to sabotage govt, says he has documents on cancelled rural projects
Article:
JASIN, Nov 3 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied allegations that he intended to sabotage the Madani Government by revealing the cancellation or postponement of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, maintained that his remarks concerning the suspension or cancellation of Letters of Acceptance (SSTs) for the projects were factual, adding that he was prepared to produce official documents to substantiate his claims.
“I had no such intention (to sabotage the government). Whether the projects have been postponed or cancelled, the fact remains that there were instructions to cancel all SSTs that have been or are due to be issued.
“I have documentary evidence of the instructions. I can show it,” he told reporters after officiating the  Mara Higher Education and TVET Tour 2026 programme in Melaka here today.
Yesterday, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer, while interjecting during a debate in the Dewan Rakyat, questioned Ahmad Zahid’s statement concerning the cancellation of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.
Rayer described the remarks as an attempt to sabotage the Madani Government. — Bernama

Title: KL steps up drainage checks ahead of rainy season to prevent flash floods, says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — Spot checks on drainage systems and cleaning works in Kuala Lumpur are being stepped up to keep drains clear and reduce the risk of flash floods, especially during the rainy season.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said these checks must be carried out thoroughly, including during the dry season, to ensure cleaning works are done properly and drainage systems function well.
She said clean-looking roads do not necessarily mean the drainage system is in good condition, as drains may be blocked without anyone noticing.
“That is why, before the rainy season, during the dry season, we have already reminded them... we must carry out spot checks,” she told reporters after launching the Community-Based Eco Recycling Hub (COB3R) at Presint 9 here today.
Hannah said each parliamentary branch office has also activated teams to conduct patrols and channel the latest reports on flash flood-prone areas to the Kuala Lumpur mayor.
She said active monitoring is crucial to ensure flash flood hotspots, which were successfully reduced from 30 to 14 over the past three years, do not rise again.
“The goal for Kuala Lumpur is to bring it down further to 10,” she added.
Hannah also said the frequency of cleaning and desilting works on Sungai Toba has increased from twice to six times a year as part of efforts to reduce the risk of flash floods.
She said changing weather patterns and extraordinary heavy rainfall require the authorities to reassess existing standard operating procedures (SOPs) and improve disaster preparedness.
“With the current weather, the current rain, we cannot use ordinary SOPs. We must be prepared,” she said, adding that Kuala Lumpur’s development planning must also adopt the sponge city approach by preserving open and green spaces to help absorb rainwater.
She said development in hilly areas must be strictly controlled to ensure the area’s natural capacity to hold rainwater is not compromised.
“You cannot replace this green space with concrete. The water needs a place to go,” she said. — Bernama

Title: MCMC opens probe into Facebook post allegedly insulting Sultan of Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has reportedly opened an investigation into a Facebook post suspected of containing highly offensive remarks against the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah.
According to
Bernama
, MCMC said in a statement today that the post was also suspected of touching on sensitivities involving race, religion and royalty (3R).
The commission said it had recorded a statement from the individual involved at the Sri Petaling police station to assist investigations.
A mobile phone and a SIM card were also seized as part of the investigation.
The case is being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, which carries a maximum fine of RM500,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
MCMC said it viewed seriously the spread of online content suspected of containing false information or insults against the royal institution, particularly material that could undermine social harmony.
The commission also reminded the public to use social media responsibly and refrain from creating or sharing content that violates Malaysian laws.

Title: Flood-hit Selangor districts back in firing line as MetMalaysia warns of torrential evening rain across 10 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an evening thunderstorm warning across large swathes of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak until 8.00pm today, a day after torrential downpours triggered widespread flash floods across the Klang Valley.
The weather alert, released at 4.10pm, warns of severe thunderstorms, heavy rainfall, and gusty winds, placing commuters and low-lying neighbourhoods on high alert following Monday’s evening travel chaos.
In the peninsula, the advisory blankets the entirety of Perlis and Kedah, alongside all three mainland districts of Penang: Seberang Perai Utara, Seberang Perai Tengah, and Seberang Perai Selatan. Perak faces widespread disruption spanning 12 districts, including Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Muallim, Batang Padang, Larut Matang, Selama, Kerian, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, and Bagan Datuk.
Across Selangor, the advisory covers Hulu Selangor, Sabak Bernam, and Kuala Selangor, alongside Petaling and Klang, two major urban districts where drainage systems were inundated during Monday’s deluge.
In the south, the alert spans Batu Pahat, Muar, Tangkak, and Kluang in Johor.
East coast states are similarly braced for stormy weather. Kelantan faces downpours across Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Pasir Puteh, and Bachok. In Terengganu, the alert covers Besut, Hulu Terengganu, Setiu, and Dungun.
Across East Malaysia, the warning covers multiple divisions in Sarawak, including Lubok Antu in Sri Aman, Sarikei, Betong, Tanjung Manis in Mukah, Asajaya and Sebuyau in Samarahan, Marudi and Telang Usan in Miri, and Belaga in Kapit. In Sabah, the bulletin spans Ranau, Papar, Penampang, Tuaran, and Kota Kinabalu along the West Coast, alongside Tambunan, Membakut, Pensiangan, and Keningau in the Interior, Kalabakan in Tawau, and Tongod in Sandakan.
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm advisories when satellite and radar indicators track rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that is either imminent or expected to persist beyond an hour. The department noted that these warnings serve as short-term alerts, valid for a maximum of six hours from issuance.
The alert follows Monday’s cloudburst that inundated arterial roads, submerged vehicles, and crippled the evening commute across the Klang Valley.
With ground saturation still high, authorities have urged motorists and residents in flood-prone zones to monitor real-time weather updates.
